articles.title: Our top 5 mini PCs under $600 for back-to-school and work
articles.text:
Back to school on a budget: Our top 5 mini PCs under $600 for work and study
Highly reviewed picks from Beelink, Minisforum, Geekom and GMKtec
We've tested over 100 mini PCs, and with back-to-school season now in swing, I've spotted plenty of deals under $600 on these compact machines that are pitch-perfect for dorm rooms and home offices, providing the performance needed for studying and working.
So, I've rounded up some of my favorite mini PC deals, including the excellent Geekom A6 for $549 (was $649), and the recently reviewed Beelink EQi Wild Cat, now $469 (was $549), both scored 4.5 stars in our review, and both are discounted at Amazon.
Whether you need an inexpensive computer for homework and browsing or something more powerful for more demanding workloads and creative projects, these are the top mini PCs you can get for less than $600 right now.
Top mini PC deals under $600
The A6 packs a Ryzen 7 6800H, Radeon 680M graphics, 16GB DDR5 RAM, a 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD, USB4, 2.5GbE, Wi-Fi 6E, and support for four 4K displays.
Read moreRead less▼
The EQi packs an Intel Wildcat Lake 304 processor, 16GB LPDDR5 RAM, 500GB UFS 3.1 storage, Thunderbolt 4, Wi-Fi 6E, 2.5GbE, and support for three 4K displays.
Read our full 4.5-star review
Read moreRead less▼
The GMKtec M5 Ultra packs a Ryzen 7 7730U, 16GB RAM, a 512GB SSD, Radeon graphics, dual 2.5GbE LAN, Wi-Fi 6E, and support for three 8K displays.
Read our 4-star review
Read moreRead less▼
DeskMini UM760 Slim packs a Ryzen 5 7640HS, Radeon 760M graphics, 16GB DDR5 RAM, a 512GB PCIe 4.0 SSD, USB4, 2.5GbE, Wi-Fi 6E, and triple-display support.
Read moreRead less▼
Geekom A5 packs a Ryzen 5 7430U, 16GB upgradable RAM, a 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD, six USB ports, an SD card slot, 8K output, and a three-year warranty.
Read our 4-star review
Read moreRead less▼
Why we recommend these mini PCs for work and study
These five hand-picked mini PCs cover a surprisingly broad range of needs, from an inexpensive back-to-school computer to something capable of handling more demanding creative work.
The Geekom A6 is one of the strongest all-rounders, combining a Ryzen 7 6800H with Radeon 680M graphics, USB4 and support for four 4K displays. Its upgradable memory and storage also give it plenty of room to grow. In his four-and-a-half-star review, our expert Alastair said it: "packs in an impressive amount of power, which is more than enough to handle MS Office and light use of Adobe Creative Suite Apps."
The Minisforum UM760 Slim is similarly capable, with a newer Ryzen 5 7640HS and Radeon 760M graphics making it a good option for productivity, creative work and some lighter gaming.
For more straightforward school and office duties, the Geekom A5 provides 16GB of upgradable RAM and a large 1TB SSD, alongside useful extras such as six USB ports and an SD card reader. In his four-star review, expert Mark said it "delivers a thoughtful design that ticks most of the general usage boxes."
The Beelink EQi takes another approach, combining Intel's Wildcat Lake 304 processor with Thunderbolt 4 and triple 4K display support in a compact package. In his four-and-a-half-star review, Alastair said: "The EQi is highly tuned to an office environment," adding, "when opening Microsoft Office, Lightroom, and browsing the internet, the speed was surprisingly sharp. The strength of this machine comes in day-to-day office work, where it excels."
Finally, the GMKtec M5 Ultra, with its eight-core Ryzen 7 7730U, dual 2.5GbE ports and triple-display support make it particularly useful for productivity, networking and home-office setups. In his four-star review, Mark said: "it supports a decent amount of memory, has dual M.2 slots and dual 2.5GbE LAN ports, which increases the number of roles that this system could occupy exponentially."
For more top-tested machines, see our guide to the best mini PCs. We've also selected the best mini PC deals this week.
Should you buy a mini PC?
✅ Buy one of these mini PCs if...
You want an affordable back-to-school computer that will spend most of its life on a desk. All five of my top picks are compact enough for a bedroom, dorm room or small study area, and you can pair them with the monitor, keyboard and mouse of your choice.
There's also enough variety here to match the machine to your workload. The Geekom A5 and Beelink EQi cover everyday studying and productivity, while the Minisforum UM760 Slim and Geekom A6 provide more performance for demanding work and even some light gaming. The GMKtec M5 Ultra is great for multitasking.
❌ Skip these mini PCs if...
You need a computer you can carry between home, school and lectures. These machines may be tiny, but you'll still need a monitor, keyboard and mouse wherever you use them, making a laptop the obvious choice for mobile working.

Wayne Williams is a freelancer writing news for TechRadar Pro. He has been writing about computers, technology, and the web for 30 years. In that time he wrote for most of the UK’s PC magazines, and launched, edited and published a number of them too.

articles.title: Una herramienta de inteligencia artificial detecta señales de acoso sexual en Roblox, la plataforma que usan 123 millones de niños cada día
articles.text:
Roblox Corporation anunció el 19 de agosto de 2026 la liberación de tres modelos de inteligencia artificial dedicados a la detección temprana de riesgos para menores en entornos digitales, una decisión que impacta a millones de usuarios y plantea un nuevo estándar de protección en la industria global del entretenimiento online. La iniciativa busca frenar el grooming, la solicitud de datos personales y las conversaciones de voz inseguras, según el comunicado oficial de la empresa.
De acuerdo con información de Fox News y el portal institucional de Roblox, la compañía puso estos modelos a disposición de la Robust Open Online Safety Tools (ROOST), una comunidad de colaboración tecnológica integrada por actores como Google, OpenAI y Discord. Esta acción facilita que otras plataformas accedan a soluciones avanzadas en protección infantil, en respuesta a la creciente preocupación por la seguridad en línea.
PUBLICIDAD
La decisión se produce en un momento de escrutinio regulatorio sobre Roblox en Estados Unidos. El Senado estadounidense inició una investigación tras reportarse 65.381 casos de presunta explotación sexual infantil en la plataforma durante 2025, el doble que en 2024, según registros oficiales y reportes recogidos por Fox News y el foro de desarrolladores de la compañía.
¿Qué modelos de inteligencia artificial ha liberado Roblox para la seguridad infantil?
Roblox ha abierto tres modelos principales de inteligencia artificial que abordan distintos aspectos de la seguridad digital para menores:
- Clasificador de Información Personal Identificable (PII Classifier): Este sistema identifica intentos de compartir o solicitar datos personales, como números de teléfono, correos electrónicos y nombres de usuario de redes sociales. También detecta estrategias para evadir filtros, incluyendo errores intencionados y fragmentación de mensajes. La versión 2.0 amplió el soporte a 189 idiomas y elevó el índice F1 de precisión del 63,41% al 90,52%, según el comunicado de Roblox.
- Roblox Sentinel: Diseñada para detectar signos tempranos de grooming o peligro infantil antes de que las conversaciones se vuelvan explícitas. Este modelo compara patrones de chat con ejemplos de interacciones seguras y peligrosas. Durante los 12 meses previos al 7 de agosto de 2026, Sentinel permitió identificar el 70% de los casos de peligro infantil reportados en la plataforma.
- Clasificador de seguridad de voz: Analiza en tiempo real las conversaciones por voz para detectar infracciones a las políticas de Roblox, como lenguaje inapropiado o solicitudes de información personal. El sistema puede suspender temporalmente el acceso al chat de voz y, en casos graves, imponer sanciones adicionales. La versión 3 abarca 30 idiomas y ocho categorías de violaciones, con un recall del 61% y una tasa de falsos positivos del 1%.
¿Qué es la comunidad ROOST y qué otras empresas participan?
La Robust Open Online Safety Tools (ROOST) es una comunidad tecnológica que promueve la colaboración en el desarrollo de sistemas de seguridad digital abiertos. Fundada en 2025 con la participación de Google, OpenAI, Discord y Roblox, la comunidad facilita el acceso de empresas y organizaciones a modelos avanzados de inteligencia artificial para la moderación de contenido y la protección de menores.
PUBLICIDAD
El objetivo de ROOST es que plataformas con recursos limitados adopten y adapten estos modelos, permitiendo elevar el estándar de seguridad en todo el ecosistema digital. Roblox indicó en su comunicado que “compartir tecnología de seguridad puede permitir que más servicios accedan a herramientas diseñadas para detectar señales de advertencia similares”, aunque cada empresa debe ajustar los modelos a sus propias necesidades y contexto.
¿Por qué Roblox decide abrir su tecnología de seguridad?
La apertura de los modelos de seguridad responde a dos factores principales. Por un lado, la necesidad de proteger a una base de usuarios predominantemente menor de edad, dado que, según datos de Roblox, el 75% de sus usuarios verificados son menores de 18 años y existen 123 millones de usuarios activos diarios en el segundo trimestre de 2026. Por otro, el aumento de incidentes y la presión regulatoria internacional.
PUBLICIDAD
El Senado de Estados Unidos exigió recientemente a la empresa la conservación de documentos internos sobre seguridad infantil, tras la duplicación de reportes de explotación en 2025. El plazo para la entrega de esta información vence el 31 de agosto de 2026, según el foro de desarrolladores de la compañía.
¿Cómo funcionan los controles parentales y la segmentación por edades en Roblox?
Roblox ha implementado controles parentales y segmentación de cuentas por edades, diferenciando niveles de acceso y comunicación según la edad del usuario. Las cuentas “Kids” (de 5 a 8 años) y “Select” (de 9 a 15 años) cuentan con filtros de chat y restricciones específicas en juegos y funciones sociales. Los padres pueden ajustar estos parámetros mediante configuraciones personalizables, lo que les permite limitar a quiénes pueden contactar sus hijos o qué tipo de contenido pueden ver.
PUBLICIDAD
La empresa recomienda revisar estos controles de manera conjunta con los menores para asegurar su eficacia y ajustar los niveles de protección a las necesidades particulares de cada familia.
¿Cuáles son los principales riesgos que enfrentan los menores en Roblox?
La plataforma enfrenta desafíos asociados a grooming, solicitudes de información personal y migración de conversaciones a aplicaciones externas con menor supervisión. Fox News informó sobre un caso en Nebraska donde un adulto contactó a dos menores en Roblox y luego continuó la conversación en Snapchat, lo que derivó en una investigación policial por abuso. Estas situaciones motivaron el refuerzo de los sistemas de inteligencia artificial y la colaboración con otras plataformas.
PUBLICIDAD
Entre los riesgos identificados se encuentran:
- Solicitudes de datos personales a través de mensajes privados o voz.
- Invitaciones para trasladar la conversación fuera de Roblox, donde las protecciones son menores.
- Lenguaje inapropiado, amenazas o acoso en chats de texto y voz.
- Intentos de evadir los filtros mediante variaciones ortográficas o fragmentación de mensajes.
¿Qué limitaciones reconocen los desarrolladores y los estudios independientes?
Aunque los modelos de inteligencia artificial mejoran la capacidad de detección de riesgos, tanto Roblox como estudios independientes advierten sobre limitaciones. Investigadores externos analizaron más de dos millones de mensajes de chat y hallaron ejemplos de grooming, acoso y compartición de información sensible que el sistema no filtró. Según el comunicado de Roblox, “incluso un modelo sofisticado de inteligencia artificial puede no detectar todas las conversaciones peligrosas”.
Por esta razón, la empresa recomienda a los padres mantener una comunicación abierta con sus hijos y enseñarles a reportar cualquier situación incómoda, además de utilizar las herramientas de bloqueo y reporte integradas en la plataforma.
PUBLICIDAD
¿Cómo impacta esta medida en el sector tecnológico y en la seguridad infantil en línea?
La decisión de Roblox de abrir sus modelos de inteligencia artificial para seguridad infantil puede influir en el desarrollo de políticas y tecnologías similares en otras plataformas digitales. La comunidad ROOST permite que empresas con menos recursos técnicos accedan y adapten modelos avanzados, lo que podría elevar el estándar de protección para millones de menores en todo el mundo.
Esta iniciativa también contribuye a la transparencia y colaboración entre empresas tecnológicas, reguladores e investigadores, quienes pueden revisar, probar y mejorar los modelos abiertos para enfrentar amenazas en evolución.
¿Qué deben hacer los padres y tutores para proteger a los menores en Roblox?
Roblox y organismos especializados recomiendan a padres y tutores:
- Tratar como señal de alerta cualquier solicitud para trasladar una conversación fuera de la plataforma.
- Establecer reglas claras sobre la compartición de información personal.
- Revisar y ajustar periódicamente los controles parentales y configuraciones de privacidad.
- Dialogar con los menores sobre los riesgos y cómo reportar conductas inapropiadas.
- Supervisar tanto las interacciones por texto como por voz, y enseñar a los menores a bloquear y reportar usuarios sospechosos.
De acuerdo con datos de la compañía, la colaboración de los padres y la educación digital en el hogar siguen siendo un complemento clave para la protección tecnológica ofrecida por los sistemas de inteligencia artificial.
PUBLICIDAD
¿Qué se puede esperar tras el lanzamiento de los nuevos modelos de seguridad?
La integración de estos modelos refuerza la capacidad de Roblox para vigilar conductas de riesgo y proteger a menores en línea, mientras ofrece soluciones accesibles para otras plataformas. Las autoridades estadounidenses mantienen la supervisión sobre la eficacia de estos mecanismos, y la comunidad tecnológica observa el impacto de la apertura del código en la seguridad infantil en internet. El avance permitirá adaptar y mejorar los sistemas frente a amenazas en constante evolución, según lo informado por la empresa y los organismos involucrados.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Internet se llena de páginas web hechas con IA: un estudio detecta un fuerte aumento desde la llegada de ChatGPT
articles.text:
Cerca de una de cada tres páginas web publicadas desde la llegada de ChatGPT presenta indicios importantes de haber sido escrita o editada con inteligencia artificial (IA), según un análisis del Pew Research Center.
El estudio refleja hasta qué punto las herramientas de IA generativa han comenzado a transformar la producción de contenidos en internet desde el lanzamiento del chatbot de OpenAI en noviembre de 2022.
PUBLICIDAD
El análisis sitúa en torno al 35 % la proporción de páginas publicadas después de la aparición de ChatGPT que muestran señales compatibles con una intervención sustancial de IA. La cifra contrasta con el 9,6 % registrado cuando se amplía el periodo de análisis a páginas publicadas entre enero de 2021 y julio de 2026, incluyendo los meses anteriores a la popularización de estos sistemas.
El resultado apunta a un cambio progresivo en la forma de producir contenidos en la web. A medida que ChatGPT y otros asistentes como Claude y Gemini se han extendido, también ha aumentado la presencia de textos que muestran patrones lingüísticos asociados con modelos de inteligencia artificial.
PUBLICIDAD
Casi medio millón de páginas analizadas
Para realizar el estudio, Pew Research Center recurrió al archivo web Common Crawl y recopiló casi 500.000 páginas escritas en inglés correspondientes a los últimos cinco años.
Posteriormente, utilizó Open Pangram, una herramienta especializada en detectar contenido generado por IA, para determinar qué páginas presentaban indicios significativos de haber sido creadas o editadas mediante estas tecnologías.
PUBLICIDAD
El organismo aclara que el resultado no significa que el 35 % de esas páginas haya sido confirmado como contenido generado íntegramente por una IA. El análisis identifica señales compatibles con una intervención importante de estas herramientas, que también pueden utilizarse para editar, reescribir o ampliar textos originalmente creados por una persona.
La tendencia, sin embargo, resulta clara. El porcentaje de páginas con estos indicios aumenta después de finales de 2022, coincidiendo con el lanzamiento de ChatGPT y la posterior expansión de otros modelos generativos.
PUBLICIDAD
Hay palabras y signos que delatan a la IA
El estudio también encontró determinados patrones de escritura que aparecen con mayor frecuencia en contenidos que muestran señales de haber sido generados o modificados por inteligencia artificial.
Uno de ellos es el guion largo, cuyo uso se ha duplicado respecto a los niveles registrados en 2023. También aumentó un 63 % la utilización de la coma de Oxford, mientras que las estructuras conocidas como paralelismo negativo, como “no es X, es Y”, se triplicaron.
PUBLICIDAD
Pew Research Center detectó además una mayor presencia de palabras como delve, interplay y testament, términos que aparecen con una frecuencia especialmente elevada en determinados textos generados por modelos de IA.
Estos elementos pueden funcionar como señales para detectar contenido generado artificialmente, pero no constituyen una prueba definitiva. El propio estudio advierte que ninguna de estas características pertenece exclusivamente a la inteligencia artificial: los seres humanos también las utilizan.
PUBLICIDAD
El contenido generado por IA crece especialmente en los .com
El análisis encontró diferencias según el tipo de dominio. Las páginas alojadas en dominios .com presentan una mayor probabilidad de mostrar indicios de haber sido escritas o editadas con IA que aquellas pertenecientes a dominios .org, .edu o .gov.
Esta diferencia puede estar relacionada con el tipo de contenidos y organizaciones que predominan en cada categoría de dominio, aunque el estudio se centra principalmente en identificar la presencia de patrones asociados con la generación mediante IA.
PUBLICIDAD
El fenómeno forma parte de una transformación más amplia de internet. Las herramientas generativas ya no se utilizan únicamente para responder preguntas o crear textos bajo demanda, sino también para producir grandes cantidades de contenido destinado directamente a páginas web.
Una transformación que comenzó con ChatGPT
El lanzamiento de ChatGPT en noviembre de 2022 marcó un punto de inflexión. Por primera vez, millones de personas tuvieron acceso sencillo a una herramienta capaz de redactar textos a partir de instrucciones relativamente simples.
PUBLICIDAD
Desde entonces, el mercado se ha ampliado con modelos y servicios de diferentes compañías, mientras que la inteligencia artificial se ha incorporado a buscadores, editores, plataformas de publicación y herramientas empresariales.
Los datos de Pew Research Center muestran ahora una consecuencia concreta de esa expansión: la IA no solo está cambiando cómo las personas buscan información en internet, sino también cómo se crea la propia información que encuentran allí.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: The Poco F8 Ultra is a denim-clad iPhone copycat that packs a punch and then some
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Poco F8 Ultra proves that 'flagship killers' can provide top-tier performance without sacrificing the norms of a great smartphone. Its cameras sparkle, the battery lasts well over a day, and HyperOS has grown into an OS anyone can use. The Poco F8 Ultra's design is clearly inspired by other flagships, but it also features some unique touches that help it stand out from the crowd — not least a formidable Bose speaker system.
Pros
- +Stellar battery life
- +Immense performance
- +Great rear cameras
Cons
- -Denim Blue is an acquired taste
- -The front camera is not the best
Why you can trust TechRadar
Poco F8 Ultra: Two-minute review
The Poco F8 Ultra demonstrates what’s possible when performance doesn’t come at a premium. Packing a top-end Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset, a huge 6,500mAh battery, and a bright 120Hz AMOLED display, it's among the very best phones on paper — but it's Poco's photography chops and unique Bose partnership that set the F8 Ultra apart from other ‘flagship killers’.
A trio of rear cameras steals the show. Poco phones (as well as those made by its parent company, Xiaomi) often sneak under the radar for photographic performance, but having shone in both day and nighttime environments during my testing, there’s rarely been any situation where the F8 Ultra’s cameras haven’t exceeded expectations. What’s more, Xiaomi’s HyperOS 3 seems to finally be fulfilling its AI-centric potential, with genuinely useful photo features that allow beginners to fine-tune their shots to perfection.
The brand's Bose partnership sets an equally high standard. While for many, the addition of a dedicated 1620 subwoofer in the phone's rear panel may seem like a token gesture, partnering it with symmetrical, dual 115F speakers quickly highlights how ‘flat’ other phones sound without external audio devices. Bass is noticeable, and the overall soundscape is more than pleasant enough to enable most to ditch the headphones entirely, so long as the situation suits!
While the F8 Ultra's design may bear a striking resemblance to that of Apple’s iPhone 17 Pro, that’s hardly a bad thing. The phone feels superb to hold and rivals its most premium opposition for style, despite its huge 6.9-inch display. The rounded corners, flat aluminum edges, and impressive thinness (7.9 or 8.3mm, depending on variant) help its size feel manageable, and it’ll quickly feel much like its more premium counterparts in everyday use. The denim-like variant is certainly an acquired taste, but I grew accustomed to it quickly and, frankly, it feels superb to use.
Under the hood, the combination of a huge 6,500mAh battery and Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset is stellar. The F8 Ultra achieves all-day battery life with ease, all while retaining superb performance under strain from gaming or multitasking. The only drawback: it does suffer from the chipset’s trademark overheating problems. While I never found the phone to be fatally hot, this temperature increase is certainly noticeable when gaming for long periods, and it can lead to some performance drops as a result.
The phone's availability is another drawback. It's available in the UK via both carriers and retailers, but only via third-party retailers like Amazon and eBay in the US. Still, the latter is more than can be said for the best Xiaomi phones, so I suppose that's a small win. The Poco F8 Ultra isn't available in Australia at the time of writing.
Poco F8 Ultra review: Price and availability
- Launched for £749 / $729
- But it's now almost always on sale
- US price varies heavily depending on the seller
The Poco F8 Ultra undercuts almost any comparable phone when it comes to price. It launched for $729 / £749 back in November 2025, but is now available for significantly less — especially in the UK — likely due to the imminent release of the Poco F9 Ultra, which is rumored to land towards the end of 2026.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
It's a win in itself to see one of Xiaomi’s devices available via Amazon or eBay in the US. It’s not available directly through carriers, though you’ll no longer have an issue using a US SIM with this device.
Even without a discount, the Poco F8 Ultra starts from the best part of $200 / £200 less than you’d normally expect to pay for a device boasting the latest chipset, triple cameras, and a huge battery. It even gets 4 years of major Android OS updates and 6 years of security updates. By which point, Xiaomi will almost certainly have released something of even better value to replace it.
Xiaomi and Poco do sell phones in Australia, but the Poco F8 Ultra isn't currently available in that region.
- Value score: 5 / 5
Poco F8 Ultra review: Specs
| Row 0 - Cell 0 | Poco F8 Ultra | 
| Dimensions | 163.33 x 8.3 x 77.82mm (Black) 163.33 x 7.9 x 77.82mm (Blue) | 
| Weight | 217g (Black), 220g (Blue) | 
| OS | Android 16 (HyperOS 3) | 
| Display | 6.9-inch 120Hz HyperRGB AMOLED | 
| Resolution | 2608 x 1200 | 
| Chipset | Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 | 
| RAM | 12GB (256GB), 16GB (512GB) | 
| Storage | 256GB, 512GB | 
| Battery | 6,500mAh | 
| Rear cameras | 50MP wide (f/1.7) + 50MP periscope telephoto (f/3.0) + 50-MP (f/2.4) ultrawide | 
| Front cameras | 32MP (f/2.2) | 
| Charging | 100W wired, 50W wireless, 22.5W reverse wireless | 
Poco F8 Ultra review: Design
- iPhone-like camera plateau design
- Super comfortable to hold despite huge size
- Denim blue choice may not be to some people’s taste
Poco adopts a reliable yet stylish look for the Poco F8 Ultra. That said, the first thing that needs discussing is its Denim Blue option.
While the material itself isn’t denim — rather, Poco's own nano-tech material — it looks and feels as though you’re texting from a pair of Levi’s. It’s no doubt a strange experience to begin with, but you’ll quickly see the benefits of this new material, namely a complete lack of scratch marks and a nice grippy feel in the hand.
If you’re after a more traditional look, there is also a black variant. It uses Poco’s ‘Glass Fibre’, which gives a feel closer to that of a glass-backed phone. It should feel less slippery to hold and pick up fewer scratches than the competition, though you’re definitely likely to see more fingerprints here than on its denim-look counterpart.
Either variant is also pleasantly comfortable to hold despite the phone's huge 6.9-inch display. The F8 Ultra has a rounded aluminum frame and only weighs 220g at most (or 217g if you choose the black version). That’s over 10g lighter than an iPhone 17 Pro Max, and yet the weight cut doesn’t leave the phone feeling any less premium when you’re holding it, nor does it feel so light that it could be easily dropped or broken.
Where the F8 Ultra and the iPhone are more similar, however, is in their shared camera plateau design. In the case of the F8 Ultra, the plateau houses not only the rear cameras but also the subwoofer that headlines the phone's Bose partnership. Unlike many plateaus, the Poco F8 Ultra’s doesn’t protrude hugely despite its more-than-capable cameras, which we’ll cover later.
Aside from these features, the F8 Ultra's design bears little to shout about, which in many ways, is a win. The denim look is certainly a unique choice should you choose it, but both this and the black variant will soon leave you thinking you possess a phone far more premium than its price tag suggests.
- Design score: 4 / 5
Poco F8 Ultra review: Display
- Bright and easily viewed
- Great refresh rate
- Simple punch-hole front-camera
The Poco F8 Ultra’s display gives the phone a premium feel from the moment you boot it up. This huge 6.9-inch 2608 x 1200 AMOLED screen is capable of a 3500-nit peak brightness, which, while lower than many equivalent phones, does a faultless job of keeping the display punchy and viewable from almost all angles.
You also get a 120Hz refresh rate to play with, meaning scrolling through social media or gaming is smooth enough for even the most serious mobile gamers. This display also offers up to 480Hz touch sampling, which gives the screen a super-responsive feel, no matter if you're gaming or switching between apps.
The Poco F8 Ultra's display is also one of Xiaomi’s ‘eye-care’ displays. These use a combination of hardware and software to reduce eye strain, headaches, and sleep problems caused by phone displays. Technologies such as high-frequency PWM dimming and circadian rhythm adjustments are employed to keep you healthy and have little to no impact on the device’s performance.
All of this technology is housed under ‘Poco Shield’ glass, which is proprietary to Xiaomi and kept for only its most premium devices. In the months of using this phone, I’ve never found reason to doubt Xiaomi’s claims of improved scratch- and impact-resistance compared to industry-standard solutions such as Corning glass. I've been able to confidently use the F8 Ultra in crowded environments without a case, where, frankly, it’s had more than one abrupt meeting with a floor.
That said, the biggest part of why this phone feels so premium to use is just how much display it gives you to play with. It has a huge 94.25% screen-to-body ratio and opts for a simple punch-hole front camera. This, partnered with its huge size, leaves the F8 Ultra's screen feeling nothing short of flagship-worthy while you're streaming, gaming, or browsing. Good job, Xiaomi.
- Display score: 4 / 5
Poco F8 Ultra review: Cameras
- Brilliant levels of detail and vibrancy
- Low-light shooting is top tier
- Selfie camera has room for improvement
The Poco F8 Ultra’s cameras are nothing short of superb — whether you use them at night, for close-ups, or even just regular shooting.
No matter the subject, the Poco F8 Ultra captured a level of vibrancy and detail in each shot that, frankly, it had no right to given its price point. Most noticeably, while shooting in cloudier conditions, shots continued to be detailed and well-balanced, without falling foul of extreme white blowouts in backgrounds.
I did find focusing on the F8 Ultra a touch more fiddly than some might like, especially when looking to shoot in dimmer, indoor environments, but with time, it becomes manageable. That said, the phone was near-flawless in picking up the subject matter and retaining razor-thin focus margins to the rest of the frame.
Each of the three main cameras is 50MP, with the phone even offering a 50MP shooting mode to make full use of these megapixels — though it sacrifices much of the camera's adaptability should you choose to use it.
One of the standout inclusions on the phone's spec sheet is its Light Fusion 950 light sensor. Taking the F8 Ultra out for some night photography proved just how beneficial the device’s 43% improvement in light sensitivity (versus the F7 Ultra) can be. Details remained sharp, backgrounds were rarely a mere abyss of black, and the vibrancy I’d seen in the daytime remained to a surprising degree.
On the front of the phone, there’s a 32MP selfie camera which does a good enough job. It definitely leaves selfies a touch smoother than you’d expect given the quality of the rear cameras, and it's sometimes a touch excessive when adjusting skin tones in bright environments. But it’s still a camera I’d happily use to snap my next night out.
Whether you’re shooting selfies or regular shots, there are also a strong number of preset modes and effects you can use to make the shot your own if you aren’t a seasoned pro. It’s not quite as many as you’d get from something like a Pixel or Galaxy phone, but the Poco F8 Ultra's camera itself proved more than capable of providing strong results no matter the subject matter, even in my amateur hands.

Poco F8 Ultra review: Performance
- Flagship-level specs provide the expected power
- Doesn’t struggle with multitasking or intense games
- Brilliant audio capabilities
It’s frustratingly difficult to fault a flagship-killer's performance when it packs a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset and DDR5X memory because, in short, it’s packing the same tech as its premium rivals, with a far smaller price tag. What’s more, there’s nothing to suggest any corners have been cut elsewhere on the F8 Ultra.
For example, I tested it with hugely demanding games such as Call of Duty: Mobile and Genshin Impact, and it never so much as dropped a frame. It’ll get a touch warm, as any phone would (including flagships), but, in fact, the alternative back panel material makes it far more manageable to hold when it does.
Day-to-day use is a doddle. Depending on the storage configuration you choose, you get either 12 or 16GB of DDR5X RAM, and 256GB or 512GB of UFS 4.1 storage. Simply put, nothing is slow to load, and you’ll likely be able to multitask however you choose to without any noticeable slowdown.
What’s more, having now spent well over six months with the device (yes, I've been testing it for a while), these performance levels haven't dropped off whatsoever. The F8 Ultra is backed by a huge 6,500mAh battery, which we’ll cover later, and it's remained a remarkably capable phone for heavy-duty gaming sessions while I'm on the go. This performance is, in part, helped by its ‘Game Turbo’ mode, though, on trying with and without this option turned on, the difference is far less noticeable than you’d expect.
Streaming on the device is something I also came to enjoy thanks in no small part to its unique Bose subwoofer system. It’s well known that regular phone speakers often return flat, unappealing soundscapes, but the F8 Ultra’s Bose partnership quite simply throws this possibility out of the window. The subwoofer allows for a 2.1-channel audio system that restores the punchiness you want while watching intense TV series or horror films (in private, please).
Of course, the F8 Ultra is no match for a proper speaker or sound system, but I’ve certainly found myself more comfortable using the phone to play music aloud or quickly watch videos while at home without connecting to a speaker separately.
- Performance score: 5 / 5
Poco F8 Ultra review: Software
- HyperOS 3 is simple enough for anyone
- AI is becoming increasingly involved in the experience
- Remains beginner-friendly without AI integrations
HyperOS has quickly matured into a clean and easy OS since its launch in late 2023. Yes, the ever-increasing amount of AI features may put off those keen to avoid extreme data collection in the name of convenience, but the software experience, regardless, is smoother than ever.
Navigating menus and finding settings and toggles throughout the device is smooth, and everything is essentially where you’d expect it to be. The functionality of some of the icon-based toggles could be clearer, but this is a problem that’s apparent across most Android OS packages nowadays.
Photo editing is so far the best use of Xiaomi’s increasing AI toolset. Beginners can quickly and easily improve their photos with an ‘AI Beautify’ tool that does a far better job than most auto-adjust photo tools I’ve come across in the past.
There are several more excessive options, such as sky adjustments, image expansion, and portrait adjustments, that may disturb photography purists, but, as yet, these tools aren’t quite as refined as they need to be for everyday use.
Outside of photography, you get several AI-based writing improvement, search, and speech tools that can be toggled to improve the everyday experience. Thankfully, having tested the Poco F8 Ultra both with and without these additions, the user experience remains simple enough if you’re keen to keep AI away from your everyday tasks.
All in all, HyperOS 3 more than matches up to the F8 Ultra’s premium specs; it provides a simple enough experience for casual users, while power users can make the most of its many customization options.
- Software score: 4 / 5
Poco F8 Ultra review: Battery
- Huge multi-day battery life
- Sub-hour charging times are very helpful
- Includes 22.5W reverse wireless charging
It’s no surprise that the Poco F8 Ultra’s battery credentials are flagship-grade. The phone packs a 6,500mAh battery with 100W wired and 50W wireless charging, and in testing, these figures resulted in months of day-long battery life and little worry about the speed of impromptu top-ups.
Slower use days will get you multiple days of battery life, which was a welcome surprise, and in truth you'll probably get beyond a day of endurance even with a reasonable amount of social media scrolling and general browsing.
Gaming and streaming were, understandably, the biggest drainers. But, even so, it would only make an hour or so’s difference to the battery life I’d come to expect. To this day, over six months later, I’m still never remotely worried I’ll run out of battery on the Poco F8 Ultra so long as I'm leaving the house with 40% charge or above.
And the phone's 100W charging makes charging a breeze. Getting back up to 100% is comfortably done in under an hour, though in my experience, it takes a tad longer than the advertised 38 minutes. 22.5W reverse wireless charging is also a handy addition for when friends find themselves in a pinch.
In my experience, you’d scarcely find better battery life at this price point. Only Poco's own Poco X8 Pro Max trumps the F8 Ultra for battery value, though you will get even better endurance from true flagships like the Oppo Find X9 Pro and OnePlus 15.
- Battery score: 5 / 5
Should you buy the Poco F8 Ultra?

| Display | Bright and smooth, it’s easy to see the Poco F8 Ultra’s premium intent as soon as you load up its huge display for the first time. | 4 / 5 | 
| Performance | Nothing seems to stop the F8 Ultra from performing. Gaming and multitasking are a breeze, with little sign of let up no matter how hard you push. | 5 / 5 | 
| Software | HyperOS is finally becoming the matured, reliable OS it was intended to be. AI is definitely a centrepiece, but it’s easy enough for anyone to use. | 4 / 5 | 
| Cameras | Vibrant, detailed, and sharp, there’s little to fault about the Poco F8 Ultra’s triple camera array. That said, there’s room for some improvement on the front. | 4 / 5 |

Buy it if
You want all-day battery life and more
The Poco F8 Ultra’s battery size, charging speed, and superb processing capabilities make multi-day use the norm — it's perfect if you’re always on the move without access to quick and easy charging.
You’re a keen mobile gamer
The mix of top-tier processing capabilities and long battery life means you can be set up for hours of high-intensity gaming. No need to turn down the graphics settings, no need to turn on battery saver; just sit down and game as you wish.
You want an immersive streaming experience
The Poco F8 Ultra’s 2.1-channel audio system and huge 6.9-inch display make for a brilliant mobile streaming experience that simply can’t be matched by any phone of a similar price.
Don’t buy it if
You want a guaranteed point-and-shoot camera experience
While the camera is superb, in some settings, the focus can be fiddly, which, if you’re after a quick shot, is less than ideal.
Poco F8 Ultra review: also consider
Oppo Find X9 Pro
Oppo’s Find X9 Pro is a step up in all the things that make the Poco F8 Ultra great. Superb photography, huge battery life, and strong performance. Just be aware that it’s regularly a more expensive choice and lacks US availability.

articles.title: Even dead websites aren't safe — experts warn hackers are spending millions on expired domains to enable malware scams
articles.text:
Even dead websites aren't safe — experts warn hackers are spending millions on expired domains to enable malware scams
A security risk that leverages existing domain trust and authority algorithms to exploit users
- Infoblox Threat Intel counted roughly 65,000 expired domains re-registered every day in the first half of 2026, close to one in five of all new registrations
- An actor it calls Sable Squirrel controls more than 10,000 domains and is estimated, by extrapolation, to have spent over $7 million buying expired names for their inherited traffic and domain authority
- Some of the domains are also used to function as command-and-control structures for existing malware that can be traced back to the same group
A domain name is the closest thing the web has to a credit history: age, inbound links, search visibility, and reputation all feed the reputation scores that security products consult before deciding whether a request is worth worrying about.
New research from Infoblox Threat Intel claims this history has become a commodity with a market price, and that at least one criminal operation has been buying it in bulk.
The study, published as a three-part series, focuses on what the industry calls dropcatch domains: names that lapsed, were released back to the registry, and were then re-registered by someone else entirely.
A dropcatch domain situation: A gambling business with a malware-enabling catch
Dropcatch domains aren't new; software has been primed to spot expiring domains for years, and it sometimes snags the occasional massive win for users who deploy such solutions.
This lets users start with domains that already have history that benefits them or flip certain domains for a price that is often a multiple of the domain's original purchase price.
Infoblox counted an average of 50,400 such re-registrations a day across generic top-level domains in the first half of 2026, rising to roughly 65,000 once country-code domains are added. That amounts to close to a fifth of all daily registrations. The rate is highest on .net and .xyz, where nearly three in ten newly observed names had a previous life, with .com behind them at 24.5%.
The problem is that not all of these are seemingly innocent or small-scale scalping operations: Infoblox has identified an entity it has labeled Sable Squirrel, part of a naming convention the company applies to domain hoarders. It controls more than 10,000 domains, most of which support a large Vietnamese-language sports piracy operation operating under brands including Xoilac, Cakhia, 90phut, Socolive, and MiTom.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Infoblox estimates the actor's total spend on expired domains at north of $7 million, which it describes as the largest domain acquisition budget it has identified for a single actor in the industry. The bigger problem is that Infoblox also found that a subset of these streaming domains runs as malware command and control while continuing to serve live football to human visitors.
More than 31,000 samples identified called back to Sable Squirrel's infrastructure, spanning Quasar RAT, AsyncRAT, DCRat, NanoCore, Remcos, and njRAT, plus samples carrying HiddenTear ransomware signatures.
Infoblox said the operator's carelessness made finding a link easier: many samples carry the actor's brand names in their Windows executable metadata, with fields reading socolive, xoilac, and 8xbet. Infoblox confirmed 405 domains as malware C2, which is roughly four percent of the total domains the organization controls, and the weaponization arrived as a single wave in late 2025 rather than as the operation's original purpose.
Sable Squirrel's core business is gambling, and while the entity tries to mask it as a streaming operation, it also doubles as an acquisition channel for the same. While law enforcement has not been silent here, it has had limited luck at best: Vietnamese authorities froze some of the flagship sites in February 2026 and charged 30 suspects in March.
They also seized assets Infoblox puts at roughly $12 million, but it seems to have survived and continues to expand, having acquired and run World Cup-centric domains since June, further expanding its footprint in a world where it has already identified and secured a large chunk of what is arguably a very important commodity: Domain authority.

articles.title: Modo Bluey en WhatsApp: cómo activarlo en cuatro pasos
articles.text:
La película de Bluey se estrena en 2027, pero eso no es impedimiento para que sus seguidores no se estén preparando para verla. En el caso de WhatsApp es posible activar el modo Bluey.
Esto hace referencia a una serie de configuraciones que permiten modificar la apariencia y experiencia de los usuarios en la app según el estilo de este dibujo animado popular entre los niños.
PUBLICIDAD
Por ejemplo, pueden modificar el fondo de los chats y el color de las burbujas para que sigan la estética de Bluey. Asimismo, pueden hacer preguntas a Meta AI sobre la película.
Cabe señalar que el modo Bluey no es una función oficial de WhatsApp, sino una serie de configuraciones que el usuario puede activar manualmente.
Cómo cambiar el fondo de los chats en WhatsApp
Para cambiar el fondo de los chats en WhatsApp en el modo Bluey, debes iniciar por descargar una imagen de tu personaje favorito. Puedes recurrir a Pinterest. Hecho esto, sigue estos pasos:
PUBLICIDAD
- Abrir la aplicación móvil
- Ir a Ajustes y luego a Apariencia.
- Seleccionar Estilo predeterminado del chat y luego Fondo.
- Pulsar Seleccionar desde Fotos.
- Escoger la foto de tu interés.
- Guardar los cambios.
Cómo cambiar el color de las burbujas en WhatsApp
Para cambiar el color de las burbujas en WhatsApp, debes seguir un proceso similar:
- En el mismo menú de Apariencia, ir a Estilo predeterminado del chat.
- Escoger Burbuja de chat.
- Optar por un color referente a Bluey.
- Guardar los cambios.
Cómo hablar con Meta AI sobre Bluey
Para hablar con Meta AI sobre Bluey, sigue estos pasos:
- Abre WhatsApp.
- Pulsa el ícono de Meta AI. Es un círculo morado.
- Iniciar un chat con Meta AI.
Algunas preguntas que se le pueden hacer a Meta AI sobre Bluey son:
- ¿Qué es Bluey y de qué trata la serie?
- ¿Quiénes son los personajes principales de Bluey y cómo se relacionan?
- ¿En qué país se produce Bluey y qué elementos culturales aparecen en la serie?
- ¿Para qué edades está pensada Bluey y por qué también engancha a adultos?
- ¿Cuáles son los episodios más recomendados para empezar a ver la serie?
- ¿Qué temas suele trabajar Bluey (familia, escuela, emociones, juego) y cómo los muestra?
- ¿Qué lecciones o aprendizajes deja Bluey para madres, padres y chicos?
- ¿Cómo representa Bluey la crianza y el rol de los adultos en el juego?
- ¿Qué diferencias hay entre Bluey, Bingo, Bandit y Chilli en personalidad y estilo?
- ¿Qué episodios hablan de frustración, celos, ansiedad o duelo, y cómo los abordan?
- ¿Qué juegos se pueden recrear en casa inspirados en Bluey (sin pantallas)?
- ¿Qué valores promueve la serie y cuáles son los más repetidos?
- ¿Qué críticas o controversias ha tenido Bluey y por qué?
- ¿Dónde se puede ver Bluey (según país) y cómo están organizadas sus temporadas?
- ¿Hay libros, videojuegos o especiales de Bluey? ¿Cuáles valen la pena?
- ¿Qué contenido similar a Bluey recomendarías para ver en familia?
Cómo crear un grupo de WhatsApp en el modo Bluey
Para crear un grupo de WhatsApp en modo Bluey, se recomienda organizarlo desde cero en la sección de contactos.
Una vez creado, conviene configurar la foto de perfil, la descripción y los roles, para que quede claro que el objetivo del grupo es coordinar el visionado de episodios y llegar a la película con la información al día.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué se sabe de la película de Bluey
BBC Studios y Walt Disney Studios, en asociación con Ludo Studio, anunciaron que la película de Bluey, de duración completa, se estrenará en cines el 6 de agosto de 2027.
El largometraje, animado en CG, estará escrito y dirigido por Joe Brumm, creador de la serie, y será producido por Ludo Studio en colaboración con BBC Studios.
PUBLICIDAD
La producción estará a cargo de Amber Naismith (con trabajos previos como Happy Feet y The LEGO Movie) y la codirección será de Richard Jeffery, quien participó en Bluey (temporadas 1 a 3).

articles.title: Canon Pixma TS6520 drops to $79 in back-to-school printer deal
articles.text:
Canon's Pixma TS6520 wireless all-in-one inkjet is a true back-to-school printer pick for $79
The impressive feature-set includes print, scan, copy, and automatic duplex printing with a 1.42-inch OLED display
Canon's Pixma line has been the default recommendation for home printing for years, and the TS6520 is the compact, back-to-school-ready all-in-one built for exactly that kind of everyday use.
Right now, the Canon Pixma TS6520 has dropped to $79 (was $150) at Amazon. This wireless color inkjet handles printing, scanning, and copying, with automatic two-sided printing to save on paper and a 1.42-inch OLED display for checking ink levels and adjusting settings without needing a phone app.
Print, scan, and copy functionality with automatic duplex (2-sided) printing, wireless connectivity through the Canon PRINT app, Apple AirPrint, and Mopria Print Service, and a 1.42-inch OLED display for monitoring ink levels and settings. Compact design intended to fit easily on a desk or shelf.
Why we recommend it
Canon's PIXMA series has built its reputation on being the printer most people default to for home use, and the TS6520 keeps that formula simple: reliable printing and scanning, automatic duplexing that saves paper without extra steps, and setup that requires little more than connecting to Wi-Fi. For students heading back to school or anyone who just wants a printer that works without fuss, that simplicity is the whole appeal.
The compact design and OLED display are nice touches at this price. Many budget all-in-ones skip a proper display entirely, and being able to check ink levels and adjust settings without opening an app on your phone is a small but genuinely convenient feature.
For more top performing units, see our guides to the best home printers, best inkjet printers, and best ink tank printers we've tested.
Also consider
Combines color printing with a flatbed scanner and copier and supports Wi-Fi and USB connectivity. Print speeds reach 11 pages per minute in black and six pages per minute in color, while maximum color resolution is 4800 x 1200 dpi.
Refillable EcoTank ink system with up to 2 years of ink included in the box, automatic document feeder (ADF) for multi-page scans and copies, fax capability, and both wireless and Ethernet connectivity. Print, scan, and copy handled through the Epson Smart Panel app.
Refillable ink tank system with 2 years of ink included in the box, print, scan, and copy functionality, and wireless connectivity over 2.4GHz Wi-Fi. Mobile printing supported through the HP Smart app.
Price Context & Historical Value
A $70.99 discount off $149.99 works out to a substantial 47 percent off, one of the larger cuts we've seen on a Canon Pixma model. Over Black Friday, it dropped to an all-time low of $64, but the general price for most of the year fluctuates between $100 and $140. So, this current discount makes this a genuinely strong back-to-school price point for an inkjet printer.
If you want to save on other units, see our round-up of this week's best printer deals.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Canon PIXMA TS6520 if...
You need a reliable, no-frills printer for school assignments and home use, you print double-sided documents often and want automatic duplexing, or you want a compact printer that doesn't take over your desk.
❌ Skip the Canon PIXMA TS6520 if...
You need an automatic document feeder for scanning multi-page documents, you print high volumes regularly and want a refillable ink tank system, or you're looking for a printer we've tested hands-on.
The Catch: What to know before you buy
We haven't reviewed this specific printer hands-on, so this recommendation leans on Canon's general reputation with the Pixma line rather than direct testing.
Like most inkjet printers, ongoing cartridge costs are worth factoring in if you print often. It also lacks an automatic document feeder (ADF), so scanning or copying multi-page documents means feeding them in one at a time.
No ADF is unlikely to be an issue for most home and student printing - we expect that feature on printers for office work and business, but it's worth mentioning.

articles.title: Oura enfrenta una demanda por las promesas sobre la precisión de sus dispositivos para medir el sueño
articles.text:
Oura enfrenta una demanda colectiva propuesta en Estados Unidos que acusa a la compañía de engañar a los consumidores sobre la precisión de sus anillos inteligentes para monitorizar el sueño.
La acción legal sostiene que los dispositivos no pueden medir directamente las señales fisiológicas necesarias para determinar con precisión la calidad del sueño y sus distintas etapas, pese a las afirmaciones utilizadas por la empresa para promocionarlos.
PUBLICIDAD
La demanda fue presentada en San Francisco por el bufete Clarkson y cuestiona especialmente las afirmaciones de Oura sobre la capacidad de sus dispositivos para identificar las diferentes fases del sueño. Según el documento judicial, la compañía habría presentado como mediciones directas lo que en realidad serían estimaciones generadas mediante inteligencia artificial.
La demanda cuestiona cómo Oura mide el sueño
Uno de los principales argumentos de la demanda es que el anillo no puede medir directamente los procesos fisiológicos necesarios para determinar en qué fase del sueño se encuentra una persona. El documento sostiene que el sueño ocurre en el cerebro y que un dispositivo colocado en el dedo no dispone de los mismos sensores utilizados en un laboratorio especializado.
PUBLICIDAD
En un estudio clínico del sueño, conocido como polisomnografía, se utilizan diferentes instrumentos para registrar la actividad cerebral, los movimientos oculares y otros parámetros fisiológicos. La demanda sostiene que Oura no dispone de esos mecanismos y, por tanto, cuestiona que pueda identificar directamente las cuatro etapas del sueño.
El documento también acusa a la compañía de utilizar algoritmos e inteligencia artificial para realizar estimaciones a partir de las señales que sí puede registrar el anillo.
PUBLICIDAD
Oura ha promocionado una alta precisión
La acción legal pone el foco en las afirmaciones comerciales utilizadas por Oura para presentar sus productos. Según la demanda, la compañía ha descrito sus anillos como dispositivos “diseñados para la precisión” y ha promocionado una “precisión sin precedentes”.
El documento también señala que Oura habría afirmado que sus anillos podían alcanzar una precisión del 79 % en determinadas mediciones y que, posteriormente, aseguró que ofrecían una precisión del 95 % al clasificar las etapas del sueño frente a los resultados obtenidos en laboratorios clínicos.
PUBLICIDAD
Para los demandantes, estas afirmaciones pueden llevar a los consumidores a interpretar que el dispositivo está realizando una medición directa y equivalente a la de un estudio médico, cuando consideran que los resultados son estimaciones.
Usuarios ya habían cuestionado los resultados
La demanda llega después de años de comentarios de usuarios en internet que han expresado dudas sobre el funcionamiento del seguimiento del sueño de los anillos Oura.
PUBLICIDAD
Algunos consumidores han relatado situaciones en las que el dispositivo calificó como óptima una noche que, según su percepción, había sido mala. Otros han cuestionado que el anillo pueda distinguir correctamente entre los diferentes ciclos y fases del sueño.
Estos testimonios forman parte del contexto utilizado para cuestionar las afirmaciones de precisión de la compañía, aunque las experiencias individuales no permiten por sí mismas determinar el funcionamiento general de la tecnología.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué reclama la demanda contra Oura
El proceso judicial busca que Oura deje de realizar afirmaciones que, según los demandantes, presentan de forma engañosa las capacidades de sus productos.
Además, solicita una orden judicial que impida a la compañía continuar promocionando los anillos mediante afirmaciones que los consumidores puedan interpretar como mediciones clínicas del sueño. La demanda también reclama una compensación económica para las personas que compraron los dispositivos basándose en esas supuestas afirmaciones.
PUBLICIDAD
El caso todavía representa acusaciones formuladas en una demanda, no una determinación judicial de que Oura haya cometido fraude o engañado a sus clientes. Será el proceso legal el que determine si las afirmaciones cuestionadas son engañosas y si los productos cumplen las prestaciones anunciadas.
La disputa pone nuevamente sobre la mesa uno de los principales límites de los dispositivos de consumo dedicados al seguimiento del sueño: diferenciar entre medir directamente una señal fisiológica y estimar un estado del organismo mediante sensores y algoritmos. Esa diferencia será uno de los elementos centrales del conflicto entre los consumidores demandantes y Oura.

articles.title: I've tested more than 100 4K Blu-ray discs, and these are my top 5 "reference quality" recommendations for showing off your TVs bright colors
articles.text:
The 5 best 4K Blu-rays for showing off your TVs vibrant colors — with titles from Disney, Universal Pictures, and Warner Bros
If you're looking for eye-popping colors, you came to the right place
In my opinion, 4K Blu-ray is easily the best way to view a movie at home. It delivers unmatched picture quality that will give the best TVs a chance to shine, along with uncompressed audio that, when played through one of the best soundbars or a full surround system, is unbeatable.
Since I started testing 4K Blu-ray for TechRadar back in November 2024 as part of the Blu-ray Bounty (where we test the latest 4K releases from each month), I’ve come to appreciate the format even more, and I've even become a fan and collector during that time. 4K Blu-ray is also a staple of my AV testing, as it uses that exceptional picture and audio I mentioned to really push AV equipment to its limits.
I’ve spoken before about my favorite discs of classic movies, as I believe 4K Blu-ray has worked wonders for some older titles. But in recent months, there’s been a few new discs that have impressed me in one area in particular: color. I’ve tested two discs in the last few weeks alone that have entered my testing disc rotation, so I thought I’d pick my top five 4K Blu-rays for color that I’ve tried out as part of the Blu-ray Bounty.
Speed Racer (2008) (Warner Bros.)
Based on the 1967 animated TV show of the same name, Speed Racer follows the story of a young man called Speed Racer (Emile Hersch), a racecar driver who follows his deceased older brother’s career and vies to become a champion. After he chooses to stay with his family’s racer company, Racer Motors, instead of joining the Royalton Industries team, he becomes a target. The movie also stars John Goodman, Susan Sarandon and Christina Ricci.
From the moment I fired up Speed Racer, I was amazed by the sheer brilliance of its colors, which practically explode on screen. Throughout the movie, there’s plenty of bold, vibrant tones that really show off your TV’s color reproduction. As the Racer family eat breakfast after the opening race, the bright orange walls, green furnishings and pink details all pop on screen. Even people’s clothes have an almost oversaturated, bright look to them than when I watched on the LG G6, one of 2026’s best OLED TVs, showing real vibrancy.
Of course, there’s the colors around the racetrack itself too. From the bright, neon advertisements to the candy-colored outfits and car decor, if your TV has good HDR peak brightness, you’ll be rewarded with punchy highlights that really dazzle on screen. The disc supports Dolby Vision, and if your TV supports it, you’ll enjoy even more vibrant colors. This really is a reference quality disc.
The Super Mario Galaxy Movie (Universal Pictures)
Sequel to 2023’s The Super Mario Bros Movie, The Super Mario Galaxy Movie follows Mario, Luigi, Peach, Yoshi and Toad as they attempt to rescue Princess Rosalina from the clutches of Bowser Jr. The voice cast includes Chris Pratt, Anya-Taylor Joy, Charlie Day and Jack Black.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Animated movies often deliver striking, eye-catching colors, but I was floored by how good The Super Mario Galaxy Movie’s colors were. It starts in the very opening scene with the Lumas. As the Lumas themselves are all a variety of vivid colors, including red, green, blue and gold, they really show the 4K disc’s superb clarity from the get-go.
There’s plenty of natural color too, particularly in Mario and Luigi’s overalls, which are the most toned down, lifelike colors throughout the movie. Scenes of space show gorgeous pink, purple and blue hues that balance that are both nicely saturated and rich, and even fire has plenty of dazzle that, on the right screen, can also look realistic. It helps that the movie has crisp textures and details, but the color is what really shows off this disc.
Wicked (Universal Pictures)
Wicked, based on the musical of the same name, is a re-imagining of the events of The Wizard of Oz. It follows the story of how Elphaba (the Wicked Witch of the West), played by Cynthia Erivo, and Glinda (the Good Witch of the North), played by Ariana Grande, strike up an unlikely friendship while at the Shiz academy.
When I first tested this disc as part of the March 2025 Blu-ray Bounty, I was impressed with its color reproduction. While I expected dynamic, lively colors, due to the setting of Oz, I was pleasantly surprised by how well the 4K disc struck the balance between vivid and true-to-life. Elphaba’s green skin, although not in itself ‘realistic’, looks believable and lifelike. Glinda’s bright, pink outfits really pop on screen, but again look natural.
One scene I frequently use in my TV testing is where Elphaba stands under a tree with pink flowers. On the right TV, this scene can really show off a TV’s colors, thanks to the vibrant pink flowers, Elphaba’s green skin and even the blue detail on the decor of the school walls. Even if a TV doesn’t have the strongest color reproduction, the scene can still look good: it just won’t have that wow-factor that does the 4K disc justice.
The Sound of Music (Disney)
One of cinema’s most iconic musicals, The Sound of Music, based on the 1959 stage musical of the same name, tells the story of a nun Maria (Julie Andrews) who is assigned as the nanny for the Von Trapp family children during wartime Austria. The movie won five Academy Awards, including Best Picture.
I’ve always been amazed about what 4K Blu-ray can do for older movies, and The Sound of Music is one of my chosen showcases for this. Not only is the restored detail exceptional, but the movie’s colors are a sight to behold. My reference scene from this disc is when Maria and the children are at a market. In front of them are various fruits, mainly yellow, orange and red, that on the 4K disc practically shimmer on screen. But like Wicked, these colors also appear natural at the same time.
Throughout the movie, many scenes of the Austrian landscape also really showcase the bold, engaging color profile that the 4K disc can show on the right screen. The green grass, gorgeous blue sky and the white snow-capped mountains all pop, and if your TV can replicate the finest details, individual shades within these large colorful areas look exceptional. This is one of the best 4K discs of an older movie I’ve seen, and its colors are a big reason for that.
The Wild Robot (Universal Pictures)
Based on the 2016 novel of the same name, The Wild Robot follows Roz, a robot sent to gather data on wildlife. Roz, who is abandoned, must adapt to her surroundings, where she becomes the surprise adopter of a wild goose. The movie stars Luipta Nyong’o, Pedro Pascal, Bill Nighy, Kit Connor and Mark Hammil among its all-star cast.
While a lot of animation, such as The Super Mario Galaxy Movie higher up this list, can opt for vibrant, saturated colors, some animated movies go for a more natural color profile. The Wild Robot is one of the best examples I’ve seen of this. Using a beautiful animation style, which looks like a watercolor painting, the 4K disc is truly stunning. Colors are vibrant, but also true to the watercolor aesthetic of the movie and really do look like a real-life painting.
There are tons of scenes to choose from here, but the opening sequences where Roz first encounters nature are the best. The green trees and fields look superb, appearing both realistic and bright, and as Roz touches a group of yellow butterflies, the screen is filled with beautiful, vivid color that can really glisten on the right TVs. There’s even excellent detail within the colors of different creature’s fur, with different shades appearing nuanced and refined. I’ve seen numerous animated 4K Blu-rays, and this is one of the very best looking around.

articles.title: Microsoft confirma que Windows 11 está provocando fallos en algunos videojuegos
articles.text:
Microsoft investiga un posible fallo de Windows 11 que estaría provocando cierres inesperados, bloqueos e incluso reinicios de algunos ordenadores mientras ejecutan videojuegos.
Los problemas comenzaron a reportarse después de la actualización KB5121003, distribuida el pasado 11 de agosto, y afectan a equipos que utilizan las versiones 24H2 y 25H2 del sistema operativo.
PUBLICIDAD
Entre los títulos señalados por los usuarios aparecen ARC Raiders y Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls, aunque todavía no está claro si el problema afecta exclusivamente a determinados juegos. En algunos casos, los cierres muestran el error EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION, seguido ocasionalmente por un reinicio automático del ordenador.
Microsoft ya ha abierto una investigación para determinar si el origen está realmente en Windows 11 o si existe algún conflicto con software o controladores de terceros. La compañía está recopilando información de los usuarios afectados antes de determinar una solución definitiva.
PUBLICIDAD
Una actualización estaría detrás de los problemas
Los primeros reportes relacionan los fallos con la instalación del parche KB5121003. Los jugadores aseguran que algunos títulos que funcionaban con normalidad comenzaron a presentar problemas después de actualizar el sistema operativo.
El comportamiento no es idéntico en todos los equipos. Mientras algunos usuarios únicamente experimentan cierres repentinos de los videojuegos, otros aseguran que el fallo termina provocando el reinicio completo del ordenador.
PUBLICIDAD
La investigación de Microsoft será determinante para establecer si existe una relación directa entre la actualización y los errores. Por ahora, la compañía no ha establecido un plazo para publicar sus conclusiones ni ha confirmado que KB5121003 sea definitivamente la causa.
El problema podría estar relacionado con los controladores
Una de las hipótesis que circulan apunta a cambios introducidos por Microsoft en la validación de identificadores del kernel. Estas modificaciones podrían estar provocando conflictos con determinados controladores que anteriormente funcionaban sin generar problemas.
PUBLICIDAD
El kernel es una de las partes fundamentales del sistema operativo, ya que se encarga de gestionar recursos y permitir la comunicación entre Windows y componentes de hardware mediante los controladores.
Si la hipótesis resulta correcta, el problema no necesariamente estaría provocado por los videojuegos en sí. Un controlador con algún defecto podría entrar en conflicto con las nuevas reglas de Windows 11 y terminar provocando el cierre del juego o incluso la inestabilidad del sistema.
PUBLICIDAD
Sin embargo, esta explicación todavía es una posibilidad y no una conclusión oficial de Microsoft.
Algunos usuarios han encontrado una solución temporal
Mientras Microsoft continúa investigando, algunos jugadores aseguran haber conseguido recuperar el funcionamiento normal de sus videojuegos después de desinstalar la actualización KB5121003.
No obstante, esta solución no funciona de la misma manera para todos. En determinados casos, los problemas vuelven a aparecer debido a un controlador defectuoso, por lo que también sería necesario identificarlo y eliminarlo o actualizarlo.
PUBLICIDAD
Quienes hayan comprobado que sus juegos vuelven a funcionar correctamente después de regresar a una versión anterior de Windows pueden optar temporalmente por pausar las actualizaciones para evitar que el parche vuelva a instalarse automáticamente.
Esta medida debe entenderse como una solución provisional y no como una recomendación general, ya que mantener Windows actualizado es importante para recibir correcciones de seguridad.
PUBLICIDAD
Microsoft todavía debe encontrar el origen del fallo
Por el momento, no existe un calendario oficial para la solución. Microsoft necesita determinar primero si KB5121003 es responsable de los errores y, en caso afirmativo, qué componente está provocando los conflictos.
La situación resulta especialmente relevante para los jugadores porque los fallos no se limitan a pequeños errores visuales: en algunos equipos pueden terminar provocando el reinicio completo del ordenador.
PUBLICIDAD
Hasta que finalice la investigación, quienes experimenten cierres, bloqueos o reinicios después de instalar KB5121003 pueden comprobar si el problema desaparece al revertir temporalmente la actualización, además de revisar los controladores instalados.
Si Microsoft confirma finalmente que el origen está en Windows 11, será necesario esperar a una nueva actualización que corrija el conflicto de forma definitiva.

articles.title: ‘I just hope this all gets fixed soon’: Google Home users criticise latest update for papering over the cracks, despite Gemini and Spotify upgrades
articles.text:
A new Gemini for Home update is rolling out, but users are slamming Google for not fixing ‘missing and broken features’ despite the voice upgrades
The complete Gemini take over is just weeks away
- Google is rolling out a new Gemini for Home update to fix voice commands for Spotify
- The company is also fixing message broadcasting and smart light controls
- Despite the upgrades, users are criticizing Google for not fixing the issues they've been experiencing for a while
The transition to Gemini has been rough — even Google knows that, but the latest Google Home update aims to tackle a handful of pain points with voice commands.
In an announcement issued yesterday (August 20), Google shared three fixes coming to the Gemini for Home voice assistant, which is still in early access. Additionally, features in the Google Home app are also tipped to get a glow-up.
The first voice command fix is for Spotify requests, which Google says has been improved to better recognize the artists, songs, and playlists you ask your Google smart speaker to play. More often than not, Gemini for Home has struggled to register commands when you ask it to launch certain playlists, while other voice commands have been interpreted as music requests.
Now, you can get your smart hub to play specific personal playlists, such as your Liked songs, and it will produce smoother results, but Google adds that Personal Results need to be enabled to request things like Liked songs and personal playlists.
As well as Spotify improvements, Google says it’s updated message broadcasting, which now works as a two-step process. The first step requires you to say ‘Hey Google, broadcast message’, and after a short wait, you can follow up with your message as a second command. Previously, you had to broadcast your message in one long voice request, so this fix removes the chance of miscommunication.
Lastly, Google is letting you be even more precise with adjusting the lighting in your home. The Gemini for Home update now lets you set your smart lights to a specific color temperature to create the perfect ambiance for a movie night or an evening soiree with friends. You can try saying, ‘Hey Google, make the living room lights 2700 kelvins,’ and your lights will change accordingly.
Useful upgrades, but there’s more to be done
Google began phasing out the old Google Assistant across its ecosystem of devices in 2025, and it will be shut down for good on Android and Wear OS devices on September 4 in favor of Gemini. The same goes for smart home devices, but the switch to Gemini for Home has been far from smooth.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Though the Spotify fixes and other voice request updates are welcomed solutions, user have called Google out for glossing over the main issues that have been plaguing their experiences, and there’s still a lot more work to be done to fix surface-level features.
Redditors who are also long-time Google Home users have shared their struggles with the transition; one user says, ‘the move to Gemini has been rough for us,’ recalling that basic household commands such as setting alarms are still hit-or-miss for them. ‘I just hope this all gets fixed soon,’ they added.
Luckily, they’re not the only one riding the struggle bus. Another user says they’re still experiencing issues with creating and scheduling basic automations for their thermostat, while a user with multiple Google devices says that Gemini is still unable to answer simple questions like ‘how long to cook a sweet potato’ — despite resetting their devices four times.
Not all the best smart speakers are perfect, but the rising reports of Gemini for Home’s ill performance are worrying for the future of Google’s smart home ecosystem. The updates are rolling out at too slow a pace, and users are already starting to lose trust.
