articles.title: Waymo doubles spending on lobbying in robotaxi battle with Uber
articles.text:
Waymo has sharply increased its lobbying spending as it seeks to persuade US regulators to clear a path for fully autonomous taxi services, intensifying its battle with rival Uber over the future of robotaxis.
The Alphabet-owned company spent more than $1 million between April and June on lobbying the federal government, more than double its outlay a year earlier, according to filings. That put Waymo’s spending close to Uber’s and well ahead of rivals including Amazon’s Zoox and Tesla.
The rise in lobbying comes as Waymo and Uber push competing visions for the future of ride-hailing. Waymo wants a faster route to fully driverless commercial services, while Uber is advocating a staggered rollout in which robotaxis operate alongside human drivers.
Their diverging legislative strategies have contributed to their relationship souring. The FT reported last month that Waymo was exploring options to exit its Uber partnership in Austin and Atlanta, where the ride-hailing group operates its services.
“They’ve both stepped up lobbying and are pushing up against each other, which now appears to be hastening their divorce,” said Walter Piecyk, an analyst at LightShed Partners.
Both companies are lobbying aggressively in several US states and Washington, DC, after pushback stalled their expansion to markets including New York and Chicago, as politicians and labour groups warn the technology could displace drivers and undercut existing services.
In the first six months of 2026, Waymo increased its spending by 93 percent from the year before to slightly more than $2 million. It has called for a federal framework to ease the rollout of robotaxis. In May, it hired law firm Greenberg Traurig to lobby on its behalf, adding to a roster of several other Washington firms.

articles.title: Proton Mail s'inspire de Gmail avec des catégories de tri automatique
articles.text:
Proton Mail ajoute un tri automatique des messages en catégories, une fonctionnalité qui n'est pas sans rappeler les services Gmail ou Outlook. Pour Proton, il s'agit de convaincre quelques internautes supplémentaires de migrer vers sa messagerie chiffrée.
Six catégories permettent désormais de distinguer les emails personnels et professionnels des newsletters, des promotions ou des confirmations automatiques. La fonction est activée par défaut pour les nouveaux comptes et proposée en option aux utilisateurs existants.
Un classement pensé autour de six familles de messages
Cette vue par catégories, Proton nous en avait donné un petit aperçu l'année dernière. L'entreprise avait lancé une vue Newsletters distincte, doublée d'un tableau de bord pour regrouper et gérer les abonnements aux lettres d'information. Chaque email entrant est désormais rangé dans l'une des six catégories suivantes : Principal pour les messages personnels, professionnels et les notifications importantes, Réseaux sociaux pour les activités liées aux plateformes sociales, Promotions pour les offres commerciales et codes de réduction, Newsletters pour le contenu non promotionnel auquel l'utilisateur a souscrit, Transactions pour les réservations, factures et commandes, et Mises à jour pour les confirmations et alertes automatisées.
L'activation se gère depuis les réglages, dans le menu "Messages et rédaction". L'utilisateur y choisit les catégories à afficher, active ou désactive les notifications pour chacune d'elles et peut afficher un compteur de messages non lus. Un email mal classé peut aussi être déplacé manuellement vers une autre catégorie. Le filtre correspondant est alors mis à jour pour les messages suivants du même expéditeur. Il reste possible de revenir à la vue classique de la boîte de réception à tout moment.
Proton précise que, contrairement à Google ou Microsoft, il ne s'agit pas de développer un modèle économique. L'éditeur suisse rappelle que chez Gmail, les onglets Promotions et Réseaux sociaux affichent des publicités, ce qui n'est pas le cas chez Proton puisque l'entreprise finance ses boîtes mail gratuites par les abonnés payants
Surout, le tri par catégories ne modifie pas la protection des messages. Le chiffrement zéro accès reste appliqué à l'ensemble de la boîte de réception, ce qui signifie que Proton n'a jamais accès en clair au contenu des messages stockés sur ses serveurs, quelle que soit la catégorie dans laquelle ils sont rangés.
Mais alors comment est-donc opéré le tri automatique ? Le classement repose sur des métadonnées telles que l'adresse de l'expéditeur, l'objet du message (qui n'a jamais été chiffré) ou certaines en-têtes du message. Mais jamais sur le contenu lui-même.
- storage1 Go de stockage
- securityChiffrement natif par défaut
- alternate_emailPas de domaine personnalisé
- smartphoneApplications iOS, Android
- push_pinJurisdiction Suisse
Proton Mail est une sérieuse alternative à Gmail. Elle redéfinit le cryptage en le plaçant à la portée de tout le monde. Certes, il faudra probablement adopter le plan payant pour en profiter au maximum, mais c'est un excellent premier choix pour quiconque souhaite commencer à s'affranchir des services des GAFAM en étant assuré que les communications restent privées.

articles.title: „Kein Bericht erzählt die ganze Geschichte“: Wie eine Plattform die Lücke bei der KI-Nutzung schließen will
articles.text:
Analyse von mehr als 24.000 Chats: Diese Plattform will zeigen, was KI-Firmen nicht verraten
Künstliche-Intelligenz-Unternehmen wie Anthropic und OpenAI veröffentlichen regelmäßig Berichte darüber, wie Menschen Produkte wie Claude und ChatGPT nutzen. Laut KI-Forscher:innen geben sie allerdings nur die Daten preis, die wir sehen sollen. „Es gibt keine unabhängige Quelle, die dies bestätigen könnte“, sagt Anka Reuel, Doktorandin der Informatik am Stanford Trustworthy AI Research (STAIR) Lab.
Reuel ist eine der Leiter:innen eines neuen Forschungsprojekts namens „AI Observatory“ (auf Deutsch: KI-Beobachtungsstation), das diese Lücke schließen soll. Die öffentliche Plattform aggregiert und analysiert echte KI-Gespräche mit beliebten Modellen wie Claude und Gemini, die mit Zustimmung der Nutzer:innen aus sieben bestehenden Datensätzen gesammelt wurden. Die „Beobachtungsstation“ soll Forscher:innen und politischen Entscheidungsträger:innen unabhängige Informationsquellen zur Verfügung stellen, um zu beurteilen, wie Menschen generative KI nutzen. Derzeit treffen die Verantwortlichen auf der Grundlage sehr begrenzter Daten weitreichende Entscheidungen über die Vorteile und Risiken der KI, so Reuel.
    
Was die Daten über die KI-Nutzung tatsächlich verraten
Durch die Datenanalyse stellten Forscher:innen von AI Observatory fest, dass sich die KI-Nutzung je nach Modell erheblich unterscheidet und sich im Laufe der Zeit verändert hat. Die Untersuchungen zeigen deutlich mehr sensible Verhaltensweisen auf, als in den Berichten großer KI-Unternehmen erfasst werden, die sich nach eigenen Angaben eher auf den beruflichen als auf den privaten Gebrauch konzentrieren.

articles.title: Pensábamos que meditar para reducir el estrés exigía demasiado tiempo. La ciencia ha demostrado que bastan unos minutos al despertar
articles.text:
Uno de los grandes deseos de muchas personas es tener un "hack" para ser más productivas o reducir la ansiedad desde primera hora de la mañana. En este caso, hay psicólogos que apuntan a que lo primero que se debe hacer por la mañana es dedicar un poco de tiempo a las preocupaciones para luego tener un pensamiento positivo. Pero hay otros métodos que están validados por la literatura científica.
No es una ciencia exacta. Ahora mismo no hay ningún estudio que valide el hecho de dedicar tres minutos por las mañanas a nuestras preocupaciones para quitarnos la ansiedad. La idea de dedicar un tiempo cronometrado a las preocupaciones y luego cambiar el chip hacia la positividad es una herramienta de psicoeducación y regulación emocional, no un resultado experimental directo de laboratorio.
La hormona del estrés. Cuando miramos a algunos métodos que funcionan de manera probada, encontramos al cortisol, que aumenta de manera radical en el momento de despertarnos para prepararnos para toda la acción del día. Sin embargo, en personas con estrés crónico, este sistema se desregula con la hormona del estrés.
Aquí múltiples estudios y metaanálisis han demostrado que las intervenciones de meditación y los programas de reducción del estrés basados en la atención plena son capaces de reducir significativamente los niveles de cortisol en sangre y saliva. De esta manera, comenzar el día con un poco de meditación bien hecha puede ser muy interesante para controlar el estrés matutino.
No hace falta mucho tiempo. Cuando hablamos de meditación, en nuestra cabeza nos podemos imaginar que hace falta dedicarle mucho tiempo para que de verdad funcione, pero nada más lejos de la realidad.
Aquí la ciencia ha visto que con prácticas breves de mindfulness (incluso de unos pocos minutos diarios) son suficientes para lograr una disminución del estrés subjetivo percibido. De esta manera no hace falta paralizar la agenda sino que una pausa estructurada es un cortocircuito eficaz contra la ansiedad.
La importancia de la mañana. Hacer una breve meditación durante la mañana o una estructuración mental tiene un efecto spillover. Es decir, los beneficios se "derraman" sobre el resto de la jornada, mejorando la autorregulación, el flujo de trabajo y la sensación de vitalidad general.
El poder de la rutina. Más allá del hábito mental, la ciencia subraya que la regularización de las rutinas diarias básicas actúa como un amortiguador. Un estudio publicado en el 2020 demostró que priorizar estas rutinas matutinas reduce drásticamente el impacto que los eventos estresantes tienen sobre nuestra salud mental.

articles.title: Apple Music terá selo para identificar músicas feitas com IA • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apple Music terá selo para identificar músicas feitas com IA
Sinalização de uso de inteligência artificial deve aparecer para usuários do serviço até o final do ano.
O Apple Music vai passar a identificar músicas criadas com ajuda de IA generativa. A sinalização será obrigatória para gravadoras e distribuidoras quando a tecnologia tiver sido usada na criação de alguma parte importante da faixa.
A plataforma enviou um comunicado a parceiros da indústria informando que o selo chegará ao serviço ainda neste ano, segundo o Hollywood Reporter, mas não há uma data oficial para que comecem a aparecer. A mudança responde a uma cobrança de entidades como a Recording Industry Assiciation of America (RIAA) e a Federação Internacional da Indústria Fonográfica (IFPI), que defendem marcações mais claras para esse tipo de conteúdo.
No Brasil, a assinatura do Apple Music passou a custar R$ 23,90 após um aumento nas assinaturas da Apple no mês passado.
A Apple já obriga desde março que distribuidoras sinalizem faixas com uso de IA através de etiquetas de transparência. Agora, essas informações devem aparecer diretamente para os ouvintes. Pelas novas regras, os criadores terão que usar as “AI Transparency Tags” sempre que a inteligência artificial tiver participação relevante na criação da música.
Entretanto, a empresa não detalhou como pretende fiscalizar os envios ou quais medidas serão aplicadas caso gravadoras e distribuidoras deixem de informar o uso da tecnologia. Sabe-se apenas que a Apple possui capacidade para isso: “desenvolvemos internamente tecnologias que nos permitem ver que tipo de música as pessoas estão enviando, e qual modelo de IA está sendo usado”, afirmou Oliver Schusser, chefe global do Apple Music, em entrevista à Billboard.
O Spotify também mantém, desde abril, um sistema voluntário de rotulagem de faixas feitas com IA. No entanto, pretende tratar essas músicas como um conteúdo separado e absolutamente opicional. A empresa anunciou neste mês que elas ficarão fora do sistema de recomendação. O Apple Music, por outro lado, não especificou se tomará medidas parecidas.
A novidade surge após uma coalizão de organizações da indústria musical se juntarem para criar um novo sistema de identifição padronizado para músicas geradas por IA. A ideia é que a tag seja similar a usada para identificar conteúdo explícito.
Em julho, o grupo propôs a criação de duas tags:
As organizações se preocupam com o aumento do volume de músicas sintéticas, que já abocanham grande fatia dos envios aos grandes serviços de streaming. Schusser afirmou em abril que um terço dos uploads mensais eram de conteúdo gerado por IA.
Isso não significa que a demanda tem sido alta: no mês seguinte, a empresa estimou que essas músicas significavam menos de 1% do total de execuções no catálogo. A maioria delas não registrava sequer uma execução.

articles.title: Slack will now let you code as a team to get those tricky tasks done
articles.text:
Slack will now let you code as a team to get those tricky tasks done
Slack Code makes coding multiplayer
- Slack Code will let workers code as a team
- Dedicated channels will let coding teams track changes in real time
- A wide range of AI agents will be available to use
Cracking those complex coding tasks could soon be a lot easier thanks to a new release from Salesforce and Slack.
The new Slack Code looks to brings AI-powered coding into the team workspace, changing how employees build and work, making coding "multiplayer".
The launch will allow teams to set up dedicated channels where teams can focus on a singular task or project, sharing it with their fellow workers to ensure nothing gets missed.
Slack Code
"We’re in the middle of a coding boom that’s changing how people build and work," a Salesforce blog post announcing the news declared, citing the popularity of coding agents such as Claude Code, Claude Tag, Devin from Cognition, GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, and Vercel.
"Now the challenge is connecting what you’re building to the conversations your team is having, all in one interface."
Slack Code will look to tackle everyday tasks such as updating a web page or fixing a bug, but is also designed for the next big project or idea. Users simply tag in their coding agent of choice, which then creates a code channel to begin.
Anyone in the channel can see the conversation, review code diffs, check live previews, give feedback, and approve the work before it ships, without the need to ever leave Slack.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Every code channel maps to one project, meaning it (should) so it stays focused and tidy, with the ability to mute or archive when it's not needed.
All users will be able to follow the work as it happens, including live previews, in their own tabs, with the ability to see exactly what has changed, with old code being struck through. When it's ready to preview, the team can watch the HTML output run live, and when a task is completed, the channel archives itself, with the record remaining as an audit log.
Organizations can tailor agent behavior and connect with existing tools, including auto-provisioning of accounts, authenticating users, and automating parts of the workflow to fit how your company works.
"Coding agents changed how individuals build. Now Slack Code changes how teams build," Salesforce's blog post adds.
"Squeezing complex, multi-turn agent work into standard threads creates noise, and letting developers retreat into private browser tabs means losing the thing that makes teams effective: shared context. Slack Code gives your team a dedicated place to work with an agent on a specific coding session or project, together, right in Slack."

articles.title: Elegoo Centauri 2 Combo review: A budget-friendly printer made even more budget-friendly
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The Centauri 2 Combo is a stripped-down version of the Centauri Carbon 2 and is a very good four-color, Core XY printer. It lacks creature comforts like lighting, a camera, and an enclosure, which greatly limits its range of filaments.
Pros
- +Less expensive
- +No cloud access required
- +Prints 95A and harder TPU with ease
Cons
- -No camera
- -No lighting
- -Spool holders do not work well with many filament spools
- -Cold plate is not sticky enough
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
The Elegoo Centauri 2 Combo is a stripped-down version of the Centauri Carbon 2, but we’re left wondering if losing the camera, lights, enclosure, and ventilation is worth the $60 you’re saving. This printer is so affordable, one wonders if Elegoo is making any profit at all.
The math and naming convention are downright puzzling. The Centauri 2 Combo is currently on sale for $319, while the single-color Centauri Carbon is $309, the Centauri Carbon 2 is $329, and the Centauri Carbon 2 Combo is $379. Forgive us if we need an evidence board and spool of red string to make sense of all this.
You’re still getting a lot of printer for your money. It’s a fast Core XY machine with the rock-solid CANVAS four-color system and a 256 mm cubed build volume. The toolhead can get to a toasty 350°C with 110°C on the bed, which is great for a bunch of technical filaments that you ultimately can use without an enclosure, but it does come in a pinch for printing less finicky high-temperature filaments like PET-GF and PCTG.
The big question is, is it worth the savings? A lot of beginners only use PLA, and see a four-color machine as a toy printing factory. But you might regret not getting that enclosure when you start getting into more practical prints and could really use the strength of an ASA print.
Ranking this printer was difficult, because yes, the print quality is great and it’s easy to use. But with so many other, even better, Centauri options available, this one just falls short of making our list of Best 3D printers.
Specifications: Elegoo Centauri 2 Combo
| Build Volume | 256 x 256 x 256 mm (10.07x10.07x10.07 inches) | 
| Material | PLA/PETG/TPU (up to 350°C) | 
| Extruder Type | Direct drive | 
| Nozzle | .4mm hardened steel | 
| Build Platform | PEI-coated steel flex plate, both smooth and textured, heated | 
| Bed Leveling | Automatic, Including Z offset | 
| Filament Runout Sensor | Yes | 
| Connectivity | LAN, WiFi, USB Flash Drive | 
| Interface | 5 inch Color touchscreen | 
| Machine Footprint | 500 x 480 x 500 mm (19.68 x 18.89 x 19.68 inches) | 
| Machine Weight | 15 kg (33.06 lbs) | 
Elegoo Centauri 2 Combo: Included in the Box
The Elegoo Centauri 2 Combo comes nicely packaged with almost everything you need to get started. There is a bag of tools, hardware, and a coil of white PLA. Noticeably absent is a nozzle wrench. There is a paper copy of the manual along with a USB stick containing a PDF of the manual and a copy of ElegooSlicer. The spool holders, touchscreen, and CANVAS system are also packed inside the printer.
Elegoo sent spools of black, red, yellow, and white PLA equipped with RFID tags to test for this review (but you'll need to buy those separately).
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Design of the Elegoo Centauri 2 Combo
The Elegoo Centauri 2 Combo is an open-frame Core XY printer with both the X and Y axes running on linear rods. The Z axis runs on three linear rods and is driven by three lead screws, belted at the bottom, driven by a single stepper motor.
The Centauri 2 Combo uses the same brass high-flow nozzle with a hardened steel insert as the rest of the Centauri line, and the hot end can get up to 350°C.
Since the printer is open frame, the single-part cooling fan in the toolhead cover is more than sufficient.
One of the only frustrating things about the Centauri 2 Combo is the filament hub attached to the top of the toolhead. The collets holding the Bowden tubes into the top are almost impossible to compress enough to remove the tubes. Elegoo has a tool that can be printed to make this easier, but it does not work well. Even if you can remove the Bowden tubes, every clog I’ve had on any of the Centauri has required the removal of the hub. On the Centauri Carbon 2, I was able to do this without removing the toolhead wiring, but not on the Centauri 2 Combo.
The toolhead wiring is a USB-C cable that is held down, inexplicably, with two Phillips-head screws. The hub is held on with two screws threaded directly into the plastic of the hub. Fortunately, the Centauri 2 Combo does not clog often, and I’ve yet to strip out the holes in the hub.
Elegoo suggests printing a one-color hub for use with TPU, and includes a press-fit collet for this purpose. However, I had no problem feeding 95A TPU directly from the CANVAS into the four-port hub. I tried using a softer TPU, and it also fed into the hub, but it ended up clogging the extruder.
The CANVAS system for four-color printing is pretty much bulletproof. The only quirk in the system is the way the spools are numbered. It makes sense for the way the filaments enter the CANVAS, but it’s easy to confuse spools three and four when assigning colors on the printer.
The spool holders on the Centauri 2 have a return spring that draws filament back onto the spool when it is retracted from the CANVAS system. They work well with many brands of filament - but not all. We had to print alternative spool holders to run Prusament and a few others that did not fit.
The Centauri 2 has a very nice 5 in touch screen with a well thought out and intuitive UI.
Assembling the Elegoo Centauri 2 Combo
The Elegoo Centauri 2 Combo is shipped mostly assembled. After removing the packing material, you must remove three screws that hold down the bed. There are stoppers attached to the lead screws that must be removed as well. The touch screen is connected via a ribbon cable and slots into place on the front of the printer without tools.
There is a bracket to mount the CANVAS system to the top of the printer with two M3x50 screws, and the CANVAS mounts to the bracket with three M3x8 screws. The filament hub attaches to the toolhead with 2 M3x6 screws, but also requires the removal of the toolhead wiring, which is attached with 2 Philips head screws. The CANVAS cable attaches with the right-angle connector going into the back of the printer and the straight one into the CANVAS. The four Bowden tubes run from the top of the CANVAS to the ports in the toolhead, and the order does not matter.
When powered up for the first time, the printer gives you a reminder to unlock the bed and remove the lead screw stoppers.
Leveling the Elegoo Centauri 2 Combo
The Elegoo Centauri 2 Combo does a self-check and full calibration when initially powered up and offers to level the printer at the start of every print. The system works perfectly.
Loading Filament on the Elegoo Centauri 2 Combo
Loading filament on the Elegoo Centauri 2 Combo is simple. For Elegoo RFID-labeled filament, the spool can be held against the reader on the CANVAS until it beeps, and then the spool can be assigned to any of the four slots. For other filament brands, the type and color must be chosen manually from the touchscreen. The filament is inserted into the Bowden tube corresponding to its spool holder. It’s easy to confuse spools three and four, with spool four being in the top rear position.
Preparing Files / Software for Elegoo Centauri 2 Combo
The Centauri Carbon 2 Combo comes with a copy of ElegooSlicer, which is based on OrcaSlicer and Bambu Studio. The program will feel like home to anyone familiar with those programs.
ElegooSlicer now features Nexprint, Elegoo’s online file sharing service, which is currently listed as beta. Nexprint allows users to select files directly from the slicer’s home screen. It currently has a more limited selection than its rivals, but should grow over time.
Printing on the Elegoo Centauri 2 Combo
The Elegoo Centauri 2 Combo comes with the usual sample of white PLA. You should go to our guide of the best filaments for 3D printing to begin printing in earnest
For the first print, I chose the pre-sliced two-color bed scraper that is included in the printer’s memory. The print took 1 hour and 30 minutes and looks fantastic in Elegoo’s red PLA and white PLA. One thing I noticed on this and other multicolor prints is that Elegoo seems to have refined the default purge values to reduce purge waste, which is very welcome.
For a large multicolor print I chose a collapsible star fidget from Makerworld. I painted it in the slicer to use all four colors on the printer and it turned out very nice using Elegoo white, black, red, and yellow PLA. Using a .2mm layer height, and running at an average of 120 mm/s, the print completed in 5 hours and 13 minutes.
I decided to fill the smooth cool plate with a bunch of small pieces, and the results weren’t great, even after using some glue stick. Fortunately, after cleaning the plate and flipping it back over to the textured side, things worked much better. I printed Leonjong’s 6 wheel antweight combat robot from printables.com. By US classes it’s called a “fairy weight” robot and fits with room to spare on the Centauri 2’s build plate. The entire plate printed perfectly on the first try and looks terrific in Polymaker’s gray HT-PLA. The print took a little over four hours, with a .2mm layer height and an average print speed of 70 mm/s.
To try out PETG, I printed a set of three funnels from Makerworld using red Polymaker PETG and the default Anycubic PETG profile. The print came out perfect, with just a tiny bit of stringing across the mouths of the funnels. With a .2mm layer height, the medium funnel took 2 hours and 30 minutes to print with an average print speed of 90 mm/s.
The large and small funnels ran together and took 4 hours and 48 minutes at the same settings.
For TPU, I tempted fate by trying some LW TPU that turned out to be way too soft for the extruder. It loaded just fine through the filament hub, but clogged in the gears almost immediately.
After clearing the problem, I printed a boomerang I found on Printables. Using a .2mm layer height and an average print speed of 50 mm/s, the print completed in 1 hour and 56 minutes. It has a few strings, but the boomerang looks great in Cookiecad pale blue elixir. Sadly, it didn’t really work when I tried tossing it around the yard. Maybe next time we’ll try PETG.
Lastly, I had to try a print that would take advantage of the high hotend temperature the Centauri 2 can reach. Polymaker’s PET-GF is a nice, semi-technical filament that is right in the sweet spot for the open frame Centauri 2. Running at 350 °C and using a modified PETG profile with 1 mm of retraction was perfect. I printed steering parts for my husband’s RC dragster that we’ll show off at 3D Printopia this fall. Using a .2mm layer height and an average print speed of 65 mm/s, the parts took 1 hour 23 minutes to print. The quality of the parts is just perfect.
Bottom Line
Currently on sale for $319, the Elegoo Centauri 2 Combo is the most budget-friendly four-color Core XY printer I’ve seen. From the well-designed UI to the rock-solid CANVAS 4-color system, the printer is really a joy to use, especially if your main interest is 3D printing colorful toys, decor, and gadgets.
For only $60 more, you can get the fully enclosed Centauri Carbon 2 Combo, which is a heck of a deal for a machine you won’t outgrow. For $10 more, you can get the single-color, fully enclosed Centauri Carbon, which is still our favorite budget 3D printer. But you have to admit, it’s quite a bargain when you compare any of the $899 Centauri printers to the current reigning champion Core XY machine, the Bambu Lab X2D, a machine with dual nozzles, five colors, and one of the best ecosystems around.
Denise Bertacchi is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware US, covering 3D printing. Denise has been crafting with PCs since she discovered Print Shop had clip art on her Apple IIe. She loves reviewing 3D printers because she can mix all her passions: printing, photography, and writing.

articles.title: Gudlyf Mobility builds the lightweight cylinders that hydrogen vehicles need to carry fuel
articles.text:
Gudlyf Mobility builds the lightweight cylinders that hydrogen vehicles need to carry fuel
The Madurai-based company designs and makes Type IV composite hydrogen cylinders rated to 700 bar for vehicles, gas distribution and industrial use.
Hydrogen has an awkward physical property. It holds more energy per kilogram than any other fuel and almost none per litre, which means a vehicle running on it has to carry gas compressed to hundreds of times atmospheric pressure. The tank stops being a container and becomes an engineering problem.
That is why cylinder design decides whether hydrogen mobility works. A steel vessel strong enough to hold 700 bar is too heavy to be worth carrying, and the weight eats the range the fuel was supposed to provide.
The industry's answer is the Type IV cylinder: a plastic liner that holds the gas, wrapped in carbon fibre composite that takes the pressure. It is the lightest of the four cylinder classes and the only one really practical for vehicles.
makes them. Incorporated in Madurai in October 2022, the company describes itself as developing Type IV hydrogen cylinders and storage systems for mobility, industrial and energy use, using what it says are proprietary materials and manufacturing processes.
Seven hundred bar, and as light as possible
The specification the company gives is 700 bar working pressure, which is the standard for fuel cell passenger vehicles. Getting there means the composite wrap has to be engineered for the shape of the vessel and the loads it sees, and then proved out through destructive testing: cylinders are burst, cycled and impact-tested until they fail, because a pressure vessel that fails in service fails violently.
Weight is the other half. The company frames its work around weight reduction for improved fuel efficiency and vehicle range, which is the whole commercial argument for Type IV over the heavier classes.
The markets it names run wider than cars. Oil and gas refineries and petrochemical plants need storage. City gas distribution networks need transport. Fuel cell vehicles, trucks, buses and locomotives need onboard tanks. And it lists aviation and aerospace, where hydrogen is being examined seriously and where weight matters more than anywhere else.
Its team is described as PhDs and specialists with a combined 120 years of experience in hydrogen storage, mobility and advanced materials, which for a company of four people means the experience is concentrated rather than distributed.
India has committed to building a hydrogen economy through the National Green Hydrogen Mission, and most of the attention has gone to producing the gas rather than moving and storing it. Storage is the part that decides whether any of it reaches a vehicle.
Awards, a university, and a very small business
The recognition it has collected comes from institutions rather than customers. It was part of the top 6 teams at the Carbon Zero Challenge run by IIT Madras and the JSW MG Motor India startup programme. It has also been an enabler at an SAE hydrogen student engineering event, and collaborates with Kalasalingam University in Tamil Nadu.
Gudlyf Mobility says it has developed and validated its cylinders and built its intellectual property entirely in India, which it presents as evidence that deep technology can be done here. No independent certification, customer or order appears in any public source.
The business behind it is small. Corporate filings record revenue of Rs 9.75 lakh for the year ended March 2024 and paid-up capital of Rs 1 lakh, with about four people. Funding has come across three rounds, none of them disclosed, with Startup India participating in April 2025.
There is also an earlier version of the company still visible. A separate Gudlyf website, last updated in 2024, describes a software business selling lithium-ion cell models built from accelerated lifecycle testing. That is a different product in a different industry, and neither site explains the shift.
(This story has been researched and compiled using publicly available information.)

articles.title: Se nos ha roto el verano y AEMET lo sabe: España va a cerrar agosto con nueve días de lluvia, granizo y fío
articles.text:
El martes 18 de agosto España marcó 43 grados en Andújar (Jaén), 42,9 en Ribadavia (Ourense) y 41,3 en Jalance (Valencia). Dos días después, medio país estaba entorno a los 20 grados.
Es decir, las temperaturas se han desplomado. El verano se ha descuidado y el otoño nos ha entrado hasta la cocina.
¿Qué ha pasado? Lo más evidente es que, como digo, los termómetros están bajando muy rápido. AEMET prevé para Burgos un paso de 35 °C el miércoles 19 a 19 °C el domingo 23: dieciséis grados. . Y este es solo un ejemplo. En Palencia, catorce. En León, Valladolid y Zamora, doce cada una. En Ávila, diez. En Galicia, unos quince grados (en 48 horas).
Son cifras espectaculares. Pero tienen truco.
¿Por qué está pasando todo esto? A nivel técnico, la explicación es sencilla: una vaguada de aire frío en altura y un frente frío atlántico se han internado en la Península con la ayuda del chorro polar. Esto ya de por sí solo provocaría una caída de las temperaturas y una serie de tormentas por todo el país.
Pero no explica una bajada tan drástica.
Lo que sí lo explica es otra cosa: que antes de la llegada de los frentes atlánticos estábamos en un momento especialmente cálido. Tener 47 estaciones de AEMET por encima de los 40 °C como pasó el martes no es algo normal y esa es la clave. La caída de temperaturas viene desde un sitio más alto de lo habitual.
¿Ya está aquí otoño? No, no. De ninguna manera. En los últimos años, el calor veraniego no ha hecho más que alargarse. Lo que estamos viendo es algo típico de la segunda mitad de agosto: un episodio de inestabilidad. Lo percibimos como raro porque, como digo, veníamos de unos meses de récord.
La mejor forma de ver que esta anomalía es temporal consiste en mirar cómo España está completamente partida en dos. Mientras el noroeste se desploma, el este de la Península sigue en aviso naranja por calor: 39 grados a la orilla del mar.
Además, esta pausa ya tiene fecha de caducidad. La predicción mensual de AEMET ya avisa de que la semana del 31 de agosto al 6 de eptiembre vuelve a "temperaturas superiores al promedio normal". Nos dan 9 días y es mucho más de lo que esperábamos. Aprovechémoslos.

Compact, sans fil et connecté, le SwitchBot Battery Circulator Fan veut trouver sa place parmi les ventilateurs d’appoint de l’été. Nous l’avons soumis à nos mesures pour voir ce qu’il a dans le souffle.

Ses commandes tactiles, sa télécommande et son app bien pensée rendent l'utilisation agréable, tandis que son oscillation horizontale et verticale permet de mieux répartir l'air. Le niveau sonore reste contenu, même à pleine puissance, et la consommation électrique est presque négligeable. La veilleuse intégrée ajoute une petite touche pratique. Reste que ce format de table impose quelques compromis. Ainsi, il faudra parfois lui trouver un support pour souffler à la bonne hauteur et la présence de pales réclame un entretien régulier. Les fonctions connectées avancées nécessitent également un hub SwitchBot. Rien de rédhibitoire, mais de quoi rappeler que ce ventilateur se destine avant tout à un usage de proximité et nomade. Dans ce rôle, il est convaincant et suffisamment efficace pour apporter un vrai gain de confort pendant l'été.

Plus ambitieux qu’un simple ventilateur de poche, le Shark ChillPill séduit par son approche 3-en-1, sa conception soignée et son format véritablement nomade. Reste que le ChillPill tient plutôt bien sa promesse : créer une bulle de fraîcheur personnelle, facile à emporter et utile dans de nombreuses situations du quotidien. Il ne remplacera évidemment pas une véritable climatisation, mais pour un trajet, une attente en plein soleil, un bureau mal ventilé ou un festival estival, il peut devenir un allié des plus appréciables.

Friday, August 21st 2026
	
		
	
	
	
Synology Introduces RackStation RS826RP+ and RS826+ NAS
Synology today announced the availability of the RS826RP+ and RS826+, compact 1U 4-bay rackmount storage systems designed to help small and medium-sized businesses efficiently manage and protect data across edge and remote environments. "RS826RP+ and RS826+ deliver dependable performance and flexible scalability in a compact form factor, making them ideal for branch offices and distributed deployments," said Susan Yen, Product Manager at Synology. "With support for network upgrades, SSD caching, and storage expansion up to 8 bays, these systems give businesses the flexibility to speeds up file access and streamlines collaboration, helping teams work more productively."
Powered by a 4-core AMD Ryzen V1500B processor, the systems deliver sequential read/write speeds of over 2,000/1,300 MB/s, helping teams accelerate file sharing, synchronization, and backup tasks across branch offices and remote sites. Four built-in 1GbE ports and a PCIe 3.0 expansion slot provide flexible networking options with support for 10/25GbE connectivity, while dual Synology M.2 SSDs via an adapter card can enable SSD caching to reduce latency.Designed with scalability and reliability in mind, the RS826RP+ and RS826+ can expand from 4 to up to 8 drive bays with the new Synology RX426 expansion unit. For maximum uptime, dual power supplies provide power redundancy in the RS826RP+, while hot-swappable drive trays and online volume management allow servicing without interrupting operation across both models.
Versatile Features for Business Workloads
Powered by Synology's DiskStation Manager (DSM), the RS826RP+ and RS826+ provide a wide range of integrated tools for modern business environments.
The RS826(RP)+ will be available starting August 12, 2026.

articles.title: Anthropic brings Mythos 5 to its Claude Security vulnerability scanner
articles.text:
Anthropic brings Mythos 5 to its Claude Security vulnerability scanner
Earlier this year, Anthropic launched Claude Security, an enterprise tool that helps development teams scan their codebase for security vulnerabilities and patch them. On Friday, the company gave Claude Security a major upgrade by bringing its Claude Mythos 5 model to the service.
In addition, Anthropic is also working with other cybersecurity companies to help them integrate Mythos 5 into their products, and it is launching a new Defender Advantage Fund (0xDAF) that will provide $35 million in credits to find and patch vulnerabilities in open source software.
Anthropic previously also launched its Cyber Verification Program, which lets vetted defenders run dual-use cybersecurity work on Opus and Sonnet with fewer blocks. Those organizations will also get safeguarded access to Claude Mythos soon, Anthropic says.
The Mythos 5 story: too good to launch
Mythos 5, of course, is the model that was so good in performing tasks in high-risk domains that Anthropic didn’t give it a public release. Instead, in June, it launched Fable 5, which is essentially Mythos 5 but with very strict guardrails.
Mythos 5, at the time, was only available to about 150 partners in Anthropic’s Project Glasswing program (and there’s the whole sidestory of Fable 5 getting banned and unbanned by the U.S. government).
Mythos 5 in Claude Security
So why does the company feel comfortable adding Mythos 5 to Claude Security now?
“The riskiest behavior occurs when a user has direct access to a model, where a malicious actor can try to steer it toward harmful uses,” Anthropic writes in the announcement. “But if users can only receive specific outputs, such as a patch for a vulnerability or a security alert, that risk is much lower. The changes we’re announcing give users greater access to the defensive results, while maintaining appropriate guardrails around direct access to the model.”
Safeguards
Essentially, since Anthropic is in charge here and all of this runs inside of its tools and harnesses, the company argues it can safely give Mythos 5 to all enterprises now. Users get findings and patches instead of direct model access, and Anthropic says Claude Security “uses Mythos 5 to scan code you own.”
It also adds that it and its partners “have abuse prevention measures in place to verify the model stays within its intended scope.”
Since many codebases include open source libraries, ownership becomes a bit of a slippery category. Also, a developer who clones a widely deployed library into a company repo and then points Mythos 5 at it would get the same findings an attacker would be looking for. That vulnerability, after all, would exist everywhere that library ships. We’ll have to see how this plays out.
In practice, this means Mythos 5 is now in public beta for all Claude Enterprise users who want to use Claude Security. Admins can enable it for their users and then developers and security teams can use it to scan their repositories with Mythos 5 at the helm and suggesting fixes when it finds an issue.
Mythos 5 tokens aren’t cheap, though. Anthropic charges $10 per million input and $50 per million output tokens.

articles.title: Günstige Tastatur fürs iPad Pro im Test: Nicht mal halb so teuer wie das Original – trotzdem gut?
articles.text:
ESR Magnetic Keyboard Case fürs iPad Pro im Test: Was kann die günstige Apple-Alternative?
Spätestens mit dem Update auf iPadOS 26 ist aus dem iPad ein vernünftiges Arbeitsgerät geworden. Apps laufen und Wunsch in frei beweglichen Fenstern. Vom Mac kommen die Statusleiste und die Bedienelemente für die Fenstersteuerung. Am besten nutzt man die Möglichkeiten unterwegs mit einem Keyboard-Case aus. Ein solches bietet Apple für fast alle aktuellen Modelle selbst an: Für die iPads Pro und Air gibt es das Magic Keyboard und für das normale iPad das Magic Keyboard Folio. Sie haben alle eines gemeinsam: Sie sind richtig teuer. 300 Euro zahlt ihr dafür mindestens.
Günstiger wird es, wenn man auf die Lösungen von Drittherstellern schaut. Das Magnet Keyboard Case von ESR sieht dem Magic Keyboard schon einmal ziemlich ähnlich, kostet aber nur rund die Hälfte. Ob es ein guter Deal ist, hängt von dem Level an Komfort ab, das ihr voraussetzt.
Kleine Nachteile gegenüber dem Original
Grundsätzlich funktioniert die Hülle ähnlich wie das Original. Das iPad hält magnetisch in der Halterung. Dadurch sieht es so aus, als würde das Tablet über den Tasten schweben. Der Winkel ist bis zu einem Grad stufenlos einstellbar. Das Scharnier wirkt gut. Da knarzt nichts und schwergängig ist es auch nicht. Und doch gibt es einen wichtigen Unterschied. Die drei sogenannten Pogo-Pins, mit denen sich ein iPad mit einer Apple-Tastatur verbindet, gibt es hier nicht. Stattdessen verbindet sich das Magnetic Keyboard Case per Bluetooth mit dem Tablet.
Das ist ein kleiner Nachteil. Über die Pins verbindet sich das iPad automatisch mit der Tastatur. Der Strom kommt vom Tablet. Nimmt man es aus der Hülle heraus, besteht auch keine Verbindung mehr. Beim ESR-Gadget muss man darauf achten, dass die Tastatur ausreichend mit Strom versorgt ist, bevor man sie mitnimmt. Außerdem bleibt sie verbunden, wenn man das iPad löst, die Tastatur aber nicht abschaltet. Da kann es schon einmal vorkommen, dass man die virtuelle Tastatur zum Surfen auf der Couch braucht, sie aber nicht auftaucht, weil das Keyboard noch gekoppelt ist – zumindest, wenn man nicht daran denkt, die Tastatur abzuschalten.
Zudem fehlt ein USB-C-Anschluss, über den sich das iPad laden lässt, wenn Zubehör wie eine externe SSD angeschlossen ist. Bei den Apple-Geräten gibt es den. Auch die ESR-Variante hat einen solchen Anschluss. Der dient aber lediglich dazu, die Tastatur zu laden, wenn der Akku leer ist. Immerhin: Die Laufzeit gibt der Hersteller mit drei Monaten ohne und zwei Wochen mit aktivierter Beleuchtung an. Im Test über drei Wochen musste ich kein einziges Mal an die Steckdose.
Das Magnetic Keyboard Case im Einsatz
Die wichtige Frage ist aber doch: Wie gut kann man mit der Tastatur arbeiten? Ich habe sie vor allem unterwegs benutzt, wenn ich statt meines Macbook Air mein noch kompakteres 11-Zoll-iPad mitgenommen habe, um auch im öffentlichen Nahverkehr, im Park oder im Café an Texten zu arbeiten oder Mails zu beantworten. Tatsächlich hat man so in der kompaktesten Sitzschale noch Platz zum Arbeiten.
Dabei ist mir aufgefallen, dass sich die Handballenablage nicht so wertig anfühlt wie beim Original. Auch die Tasten bieten durch ihren gummierten Überzug guten Grip, beim Magic Keyboard ist das Feeling aber noch mal ein anderes. Dafür stimmt der Hub. Trotz der flachen Basis lässt sich angenehm auf dem Keyboard tippen. Geräusche gibt es dabei kaum. Wer den kleckernden Sound beim Schreiben braucht, ist hier also falsch.
Obwohl der Platz bei einem 11-Zoll-Tablet sehr endlich ist, wirkt das Layout der Tastatur etwas zu gedrungen. Die beiden Shift-Tasten nehmen viel Platz ein, rechts ist zu erkennen, dass ein US-Layout schlicht auf Deutsch umgelabelt wurde. Insbesondere Umlaute und die Pfeiltasten sind etwas klein geraten. Bevor man blind darauf schreiben kann, vergeht etwas Zeit.
Eigene Funktionstasten hat das Keyboard. Sie sind auf der Zahlenreihe doppelt belegt. Um die Lautstärke oder die Helligkeit am iPad zu regeln, müsst ihr entsprechend die Fn-Taste bemühen. Über weitere regelt ihr die Medienwiedergabe, schaltet das Mikrofon stumm oder wählt zwischen den Farben der Beleuchtung aus. Dabei erinnert die Tastatur eher an ein Keyboard für Gamer:innen und weniger an ein Werkzeug für Web-Worker. Eine normale weiße Beleuchtung gehört nämlich nicht zum Umfang. Das ist Geschmackssache.
Gelungen ist das Trackpad. Es ist schön breit, unterstützt alle üblichen Gesten und lässt sich überall klicken. Das klingt zwar etwas hohl, es stört aber auch nicht weiter. Insgesamt kann man damit flott und einfach durch die Menüs wischen.
Fazit
Das Magnetic Keyboard Case von ESR ist nicht ganz genauso gut wie das Magic Keyboard von Apple. Dafür fühlt sich das Original zu sehr nach Premium an. Das schlägt sich allerdings auch im Preis nieder. 349 Euro für die Version fürs dünne iPad Pro mit M4- oder M5-Chip muss man erstmal übrig haben. Rechnet man den Preis für Tablet und Tastatur zusammen, ist man immerhin schnell in Macbook-Sphären unterwegs.
Das ESR-Keyboard kostet in dieser Ausführung fürs iPad Pro M1 oder M2 bei Amazon aktuell rund 100 Euro. Es ist damit also deutlich günstiger als das Original. Sieht es aus wie eine Kopie? Aber, hallo. Lässt sich damit gut arbeiten? Das geht, nach kurzer Eingewöhnung, auf jeden Fall auch. Wenn es nicht zwingend das Apple-Logo auf der Rückseite sein muss, ist das Magnetic Keyboard Case eine gelungene und günstige Alternative.

articles.title: As demand for Meta AI glasses explodes, it’s harder to avoid creepy recordings
articles.text:
Can you tell when someone nearby is wearing Meta AI glasses?
As millions of people buy into the smart glasses fad each year, the odds are increasing that you could be secretly recorded while simply going about your day.
Meta is not the only smart glasses maker, but its AI glasses are by far the most popular. And as the devices become more common, some public places, including schools, courts, restaurants, and entertainment venues, have begun to ban them. Even tech lovers have rejected Meta glasses in certain settings. The hackers behind DEF CON 2026 reportedly banned smart glasses with no exceptions, reminding attendees with prescription pairs to “be sure to pack non-violating eyewear if you need them.”
But a ban is only as effective as the people enforcing it. Spotting a pair of smart glasses can require tech-savvy security staff, and enforcement may depend on users voluntarily disclosing their devices—or on watchful observers speaking up.
Those bans are an important way to push back against the potential for abuse. But privacy advocates know that increasing the social friction around nonconsensual recording can’t stop the practice by itself.
Until comprehensive consumer privacy laws are passed, the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) has warned that Meta seems prepared to make the tech even more invasive in its bid to sell more glasses and stay ahead of rivals in the burgeoning industry.
And as AI advances, EFF staff technologist Cooper Quintin told Ars, potential new features such as facial recognition could raise the stakes further, potentially allowing the devices to be used to create convincing deepfakes or nonconsensual intimate imagery of people who may not be aware that cameras are rolling.
“I think that there are a lot of other concerns there beyond just being recorded without your knowledge,” Quintin told Ars.
EFF has warned that smart glasses makers will likely be tempted to add facial-recognition features unless lawmakers intervene and give people a private right to sue companies whose products violate their biometric privacy rights. In the meantime, the group has released a guide for smart-glasses users that lays out ways to resist facial recognition, develop responsible recording habits, and better understand the privacy risks of continuous recording. It also urges users to consider blurring strangers’ faces before posting videos online.
For people unknowingly targeted in secret recordings, the only safety feature Meta provides is nearly “useless,” Quintin told Ars.
A tiny recording light that can be easily covered with a sticker is unlikely to deter bad actors intent on abusing the glasses, whether that’s stalkers or creepy partners secretly recording women in public bathrooms or private bedrooms. The tech has also controversially been used in immigration raids, 404 Media reported, and to harass sex workers and retail workers. And on social media, videos show a range of other unwanted recordings, from relatively inoffensive pranks to more harmful videos featuring bullying or harassment.
The volume of these videos online suggests the LED feature “is better than nothing, but not by much,” Quintin said.
Hobbyists build apps to detect glasses
Experts have noted that Meta may already have plans to diminish that limited safety feature. The company is supposedly “testing a prototype of ‘super sensing’ AI glasses that would use cameras and audio recordings to capture a wearer’s every moment,” the Financial Times reported last month. According to sources familiar with Meta’s thinking, executives “are planning not to activate the LED when the super-sensing features are being used,” even though “that would make it harder for bystanders to know when they were being recorded.”
Meta execs’ plans may change if the public’s privacy concerns remain a sticking point, though, sources have suggested. And backlash will likely be sustained as more people wear the glasses, since digital rights experts have accused Meta of failing to consider civil rights or privacy ramifications when designing new features. Perhaps most troublingly, Meta recently backpedaled and deleted an unreleased facial recognition system from its smart-glasses app that Wired and EFF revealed had been quietly installed on 50 million phones in June.
It’s unclear if or when Meta might try to bring the facial recognition system back. Meta did not respond to Ars’ request to comment on this story.
As Meta glasses have become more commonplace, hobbyist programmers have been building apps to detect when smart glasses are nearby so people can steer clear of them.
These civil defense apps, Quintin said, aren’t a perfect solution to the social problem of smart-glasses recording without consent. But when used in combination with bans, the apps can offer wary members of the public a way to check if a ban is being enforced or whether a nearby device may begin recording at a sensitive time. Society needs both solutions, Quintin said, especially because the most popular and recognizable smart glasses available today will likely one day come in a wider assortment of trendy models, making them harder to spot in the wild.
“You need to have the social construct around these being unwelcome, and you also need to be able to find when people are using these,” Quintin said. “Right now, they’re pretty easy to just detect with your eyes. They’re pretty obvious, but that might not always be the case. So technologies like this are also important to supplement that.”
“I can do something about it”
Since February, engineers have been releasing and updating apps that help people detect glasses like Ray-Ban Meta, Oakley Meta, or Snap Spectacles.
“It is completely unsurprising that people are building apps to fight back against Meta glasses and other surreptitious public recording,” Quintin told Ars. Many people “have a deep revulsion to being recorded without their consent, which is understandable,” and that remains “the biggest problem with these glasses,” Quintin said.
Smart-glasses detector apps aren’t perfect. At best, they can alert users when nearby glasses are turned on by detecting the Bluetooth signal used to pair the glasses with a phone. Most importantly, the apps cannot determine whether the glasses are actively recording, and users are cautioned to never assume that someone wearing smart glasses is recording them. App makers also advise against confrontation and accept no liability for false positives or misunderstandings. Additionally, detection may be unreliable if a wall or other obstacle, like a human body, interferes with a signal.
Users don’t seem to consider these flaws deal-breakers. They simply want some way to scan a room, and some are eager to provide feedback to improve the apps, even expressing an emotional investment in seeing the technology develop.
One of the first apps, Nearby Glasses, is available for $2.99 on both iOS and Android. It has been downloaded more than 100,000 times from the Play Store and remains the most popular such app, despite the developer, Yves Jeanrenaud, warning on GitHub that he’s “no pro developer” and that “detecting Bluetooth LE devices might sometimes just not work as expected,” and “false positives are likely.”
Released in response to online content showing that smart glasses are “an intolerable intrusion, consent neglecting, horrible piece of tech,” Jeanrenaud said, he kept his goals humble. On GitHub, he wrote, “I hope this app is useful for someone,” but “I do not want to promote techsolutionism, nor do I want people to feel falsely secure. It’s still an imperfect approach,” and it probably “always will be.”
By July, another detector, Antizuck Smart Glasses Scanner, was nearing the top of iPhone charts, also charging $3 for the service. One high school teacher reviewing the app called it the “best $3 I’ve spent,” writing that she was concerned that her students could use AI glasses to take unwanted recordings in class.
Ars tested the most recently released app, Zuckoff, which launched for free on iPhone in early August and is currently seeking 12 testers to launch on Android devices later this year.
Already, thousands of users have downloaded the iPhone app, with some eagerly submitting feedback that has helped improve key functionality, including the ability to detect AI glasses and receive alerts when the app is closed. Perpetual scanning is an optional feature that costs about $10 a year. The subscription helps cover the costs of “continuous support” for the app, Zuckoff’s creator, Pawel Szydlowski, told Ars.
Like Jeanrenaud’s app, Zuckoff collects no data and was created partly in response to the toxic Meta glasses content that is flooding social media. Szydlowski told Ars that he built the app in one week after finishing another project that scans for nearby Bluetooth devices and deciding, “Let’s see how far we can go with detecting those glasses.”
Without researching whether other apps had already sought to solve the problem, Szydlowski decided to put his 10 years of iPhone developer experience to work. “I was like, ‘I can do something about it, so let’s go,’” Szydlowski told Ars.
Building a Meta glasses detector
Szydlowski’s biggest challenge was collecting the unique identifiers that manufacturers use to label different products for regulatory purposes. Zuckoff uses these identifiers to help users detect specific smart-glasses models while ignoring Bluetooth signals from less creepy devices. To compile as comprehensive a list as possible, Szydlowski crawled Instagram and Reddit for photos of people wearing different types of smart glasses.
“I see you have those glasses,” Szydlowski would say in messages to early Meta glasses adopters, who agreed to help despite presumably approving of the technology. “Can you help me with this little name? I want to know the unique identifier that’s broadcasting.”
To catch glasses with identifiers that Zuckoff hasn’t yet logged, Szydlowski created a workaround that first flags devices by their advertised names. It’s less precise, he said, but it gives users some indication that a pair of smart glasses may be nearby, even without a known identifier. He’s currently working on another solution that should widen discovery even further, he told Ars.
Szydlowski’s app first alerted him to nearby smart glasses when he ran into two colleagues wearing them at a recent Apple event in Poland. That helped him confirm the tech was working as he hoped.
When you load Zuckoff, the app “estimates distance from signal strength and puts a confidence level on every hit rather than a hard yes or no,” Szydlowski explained. Estimates tell users if glasses are very close (within arm’s length), close (in the same room), near (nearby), and far. This feature also makes it possible to see when you may be approaching an area with a larger concentration of smart glasses, like in a tourist trap like the Las Vegas strip.
Ars replicated the test, thanks to this writer’s brother-in-law, who agreed to use the app to detect his own Ray-Bans. He likes to use his smart glasses to record nature sightings when he goes boating or to take action shots of his bulldog playing fetch along the lake, and he had the glasses on him when I called to see if he could run the test.
After putting the glasses on, my brother-in-law loaded the app, which detected the glasses in minutes and warned that “one possible pair” was “within arm’s length.” (In this case, the message was very literal, since he was wearing the glasses while looking at the phone in his hand.)
The app then references the identifier to help the user detect exactly which model is nearby, and my brother-in-law confirmed that Zuckoff correctly labeled his smart glasses.
For Szydlowski, the toughest challenge was figuring out how Apple might allow the app to run in the background, since the company is “very strict when it comes to apps working in the background all the time.” He worried some users wouldn’t find the app as beneficial without that functionality. Eventually, he settled on a solution that scans continuously, but rather than flagging all known devices the moment they’re turned on, Apple allows only a fixed list of known Bluetooth service identifiers to be detected in that mode. Extra-cautious users should therefore also open the app to see the full list of potential devices in the area.
“This background feature, it’s so crucial,” Szydlowski said.
Android may allow him to offer faster detection through background functionality, Szydlowski suggested, because unlike Apple devices, Android allows background activities to be “possible to exempt from battery optimization,” Szydlowski said. That means Zuckoff “can continue using the battery in the background” without Android protocols that “wipe out the apps that are consuming your battery,” he said.
Although people have mostly grown accustomed to the idea of being recorded without consent in public, smart glasses have the potential to expand mass surveillance in ways that deeply concern privacy advocates.
Meta could introduce technical solutions, like automatically blurring faces, as Google does in Street View images, but Szydlowski doubts Meta would voluntarily make such a privacy-conscious change without regulatory or public pressure. The creator of Zuckoff, a name that takes a cheeky dig at Meta’s founder, also said that “I’m pretty sure they’re not going to be happy with this app existing.”
He likens malicious smart-glasses recording to the earliest harms of Apple’s AirTags. When that technology was released in 2021, the easy-to-hide tracking devices were soon implicated in stalking cases. But there still is no federal law targeting AirTag abuses, and it took the first states to act on the emerging privacy threat roughly three to five years to pass legislation to prohibit the invasive tracking.
Szydlowski worries lawmakers will be similarly slow to react to threats from Meta glasses. He told Ars he thinks the best solution might be rules mandating companies like Meta advertise a specific Bluetooth service identifier while recording. That would improve civil defense apps like his.
In the meantime, he hopes people will find the detector app that they like best and use it to spread awareness that smart glasses may be present in a room where they’re unexpected or explicitly forbidden.
“The goal of this app was just making people aware because a lot of people won’t be aware until it becomes a major problem, which was the case with AirTags, basically,” Szydlowski said.
Meta expects demand to explode
Last December, analysts forecasted that 2026 would be a breakthrough year for smart glasses. And it’s clear by now that Meta wants this to be the year that AI glasses are suddenly everywhere you look.
The tech giant invested heavily in promoting them, collaborating with celebrity influencer Kylie Jenner on a pair of Ray-Bans featuring an AI assistant that speaks in her voice. The campaign featured billboard ads and a video spot showing Kylie simply enjoying wearing the glasses, without necessarily highlighting their practical features. The partnership was rumored to have paid Jenner millions of dollars and was intended to position the technology as a fashionable, practical accessory—and perhaps buff out the public perception of them as “pervert glasses.” But critics have argued that the ads seem narrowly designed to encourage more people to use their glasses for continuous recording.
Though the Jenner campaign was supposedly viewed as a success internally at Meta, it also prompted global backlash. On social media, the protest collective “Everyone Hates Elon” razed Jenner, The Huffington Post reported, saying that “recording everything we see and do constantly? It’s giving fascism, not fashion, hun.” And pop singer Lorde stopped a festival performance to tell her fans, “Fuck the glasses. Don’t get the glasses. Not sexy.”
Salon’s Andi Zeisler slammed the Kylie Edition glasses for trying to lull women into a false sense of security, even as Meta knows the technology has been used to record women without their knowledge, both in public and private. In London, activists took that criticism a step further, replacing bus stop ads of Jenner smiling in the glasses with a spoof in which her face transforms into a skeletal grin above the warning that at Meta, “We’re always watching.”
But despite protests, the glasses aren’t going away any time soon, as Meta plans to move millions more into production. In 2025, the company sold more than 7 million AI glasses—up from 2 million sold in the prior two years combined—then quickly made plans to double its Ray-Ban outputs, Bloomberg reported. By the end of 2026, Meta expects to start producing at least 20 million glasses annually to meet demand, or perhaps as many as 30 million if the market continues trending strongly.
Beyond the backlash, regulating the glasses is a touchy subject, Quintin told Ars. No civil rights group would advocate banning recording in public, a practice that can be crucial for holding police and government officials accountable. What may prove just as useful as thoughtful privacy regulations, Quintin suggested, is a broader effort to ban the technology at the community level.
Szydlowski told Ars that he’s personally not bothered by Meta’s AI glasses, only by the gross content made with them. But other critics, like Quintin, think the tech is “disgusting” and “unacceptable,” and he has little hope that technical solutions can solve the problem and abundant concern that the privacy risks will compound as enthusiasm for the technology grows.
Right now, there’s less social friction around using glasses to record than there was when people first started using phones to record public interactions, Quintin suggested. As a father of young children, he recently saw another dad using glasses to film kids at a birthday party, a moment that illustrates how smart glasses have shifted the power dynamic.
Previously, “if you wanted to record somebody, you had to take out your phone, shove it in their face,” Quintin said. “And they know they’re being recorded. That is a useful social friction. And the glasses remove that and put the friction on the other end. The friction is now on me, calling you a pervert for wearing glasses and telling you to stop recording my kids.”
Szydlowski somewhat agreed. He told Ars there’s value in being able to record hands-free from eye level, but he created Zuckoff because he draws the line at posting harmful smart-glasses recordings online.
“People are using it in a bad way,” Szydlowski said. “That was the first part that annoyed me. I was like, ‘I don’t like it. I just don’t enjoy the content, and I don’t think it’s valid,’ because myself, I wouldn’t have a way to react to being recorded because I’m used to people holding the phone and actually pointing at me. Then I can say, ‘Hold on a second. This is not scrolling. Someone is actually recording.’”
Ashley is a senior policy reporter for Ars Technica, dedicated to tracking social impacts of emerging policies and new technologies. She is a Chicago-based journalist with 20 years of experience.

articles.title: Huawei Watch Fit 5 com função mini treino chega a 54% OFF no Mercado Livre • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Huawei Watch Fit 5 com função mini treino chega a 54% OFF no Mercado Livre
Watch Fit 5 tem tela AMOLED de 2.500 nits e função mini treino para até 10 partes do corpo; smartwatch da Huawei recebe desconto de 54% no Pix com cupom
O Watch Fit 5 está saindo por R$ 692 no Pix com cupom MAISECONOMIA no Mercado Livre. O smartwatch da Huawei, com tela AMOLED de até 2.500 nits e modo de mini treino que suporta exercícios localizados para partes específicas do corpo, recebe um desconto de 54% sobre o preço original de R$ 1.499.
O Watch Fit 5 é um dos lançamentos mais recentes da Huawei. Ele possui uma ampla tela AMOLED de 1,82″ e brilho forte de até 2.500 nits, capaz de reproduzir imagens com alta qualidade de cores, além de garantir a visibilidade em qualquer ambiente.
Seus sensores avançados suportam várias modalidades esportivas diferentes, com destaque para o modo de mini treino para exercícios localizados de 10 partes do corpo, como cabeça e pescoço. O gadget possui também funções de qualidade de vida, como monitoramento do sono, saúde da mulher e oxigenação do sangue.
Este acessório também pode fazer a diferença em uma situação crítica: após uma queda e caso o usuário não se recupere sozinho, o relógio inteligente pode disparar chamadas para contatos pré-gravados e números de emergência, desde que esteja pareado a um celular.
O corpo de alumínio com traseira de plástico do wearable possui certificação IP6X, que oferece resistência contra poeira intensa, mas não tem proteção comprovada contra líquidos. Ainda assim, a fabricante diz que ele pode ser usado em piscinas rasas ou na costa marítima, mas que o usuário evite usá-lo em mergulhos.
Sua bateria de 471 mAh oferece até 10 dias de uso moderado segundo a Huawei, assim permitindo que o gadget seja usado por longos períodos sem se preocupar com tomadas e carregadores.
O Huawei Watch Fit 5 (R$ 692 no Pix com cupom MAISECONOMIA) possui conectividade Bluetooth 6.0, BLE e GPS multibanda, que determina a posição do usuário em tempo real. O acessório é compatível tanto com iPhones (com algumas limitações) quanto com smartphones Android.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: Understanding infrastructure performance is becoming more important than ever
articles.text:
Understanding infrastructure performance is becoming more important than ever
Critical infrastructure faces a common challenge
Critical infrastructure faces a common challenge. Across transport, utilities and communications, organizations are expected to deliver higher levels of performance, resilience and security while working with ageing assets and increasingly constrained budgets.
Large-scale replacement programs are rarely practical, affordable or necessary.
Instead, the organizations making the greatest progress are taking a different approach. They are building a much deeper understanding of the IT infrastructure they already own, using data and operational insight to improve performance, target investment and extend asset life.
Group Engineering Director at Telent.
This shift reflects a broader change in how infrastructure is managed. Rather than asking what needs replacing, operators are asking how existing IT assets can deliver more value.
Intelligent Infrastructure is helping answer that question by connecting assets, improving visibility and enabling better operational decisions.
For organizations responsible for critical infrastructure, success increasingly depends on understanding what is already in place, optimizing its performance and ensuring every investment delivers measurable value.
Different sectors, the same infrastructure challenge
While the infrastructure itself may differ between sectors, many of the challenges facing operators today are remarkably similar.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Whether managing a rail network, a water treatment facility, an electricity distribution network or a communications system, there is growing pressure to improve performance while operating within increasingly constrained budgets. At the same time, expectations around reliability, resilience and cybersecurity continue to rise, with customers and stakeholders expecting services to be available whenever they are needed.
Many organizations are also reliant on infrastructure that has been in operation for decades. In some cases, assets are performing well beyond their original design life. Replacing them is often costly, disruptive and difficult to justify when investment priorities are competing for limited resources.
Alongside this, operators are being asked to meet wider sustainability objectives, reduce unnecessary site visits and make better use of the resources available to them. The result is a complex balancing act between maintaining existing infrastructure, delivering operational improvements and planning for future requirements.
These challenges are not unique to one industry, and many organizations are asking the same questions. How can they improve resilience without significantly increasing costs? How can they make better use of existing assets? How can they prioritize investment with greater confidence? And how can they continue to meet rising expectations while working within finite resources?
Finding the answers starts with understanding infrastructure performance in greater detail. Not simply knowing whether an asset is operational, but understanding how it is performing, how its performance changes over time and what those changes might indicate. As infrastructure networks become larger, more connected and increasingly complex, that level of understanding is becoming essential.
Why understanding asset performance has become a strategic advantage
Infrastructure operators have never had access to more information about their assets than they do today. Connected devices, sensors and operational systems continuously generate information about the condition and performance of infrastructure. The opportunity now lies in making better use of that information to gain meaningful understanding to enable operational decision making, supporting desired business outcomes.
For many organizations, operational data exists across multiple systems, technologies and teams. Individual systems may provide valuable insight into specific assets, but they rarely provide a complete view of how the wider infrastructure network is performing. This can make it difficult to identify emerging issues, understand relationships between assets or recognize changes in performance before they begin to affect service delivery.
This becomes even more challenging where infrastructure has evolved over many years and comprises different technologies from multiple manufacturers. Legacy systems often operate alongside newer technologies, with each generating its own data and requiring its own management processes. Bringing these different sources of information together provides a far richer understanding of how infrastructure is performing.
Greater visibility allows operators to move beyond simply reacting to faults. It creates an opportunity to understand what normal performance looks like, identify trends over time and recognize when assets begin operating outside expected parameters. In many cases, these early indicators provide valuable time to investigate, prioritize activity and resolve issues before they affect customers or critical services.
This is where Intelligent Infrastructure begins to deliver real value. By securely connecting assets, bringing together operational data and providing a clearer understanding of infrastructure performance, organizations are better equipped to make informed decisions about how networks are managed, maintained and developed.
From operational insight to better decisions
Traditionally, many maintenance programs have been built around routine inspection schedules or simply responding to faults after they occur. While these approaches continue to play an important role, they do not always reflect the actual condition of assets or where engineering effort will have the greatest impact.
A clearer understanding of infrastructure performance allows operators to take a more informed and prognostic approach. Maintenance activities can be prioritized according to operational need, performance trends and potential risk rather than treating every asset in the same way. Engineering teams are able to focus their attention where it will deliver the greatest benefit, while emerging issues can be investigated before they develop into larger operational problems.
Over time, this supports a more informed approach to asset management. Maintenance ceases to be reactive and becomes increasingly proactive driven by the condition and performance of assets rather than fixed schedules alone. This can help reduce unplanned outages, improve network resilience and minimize disruption for customers and end users.
The benefits extend well beyond day-to-day operations. Better insight into infrastructure performance also supports longer-term planning by helping organizations understand where investment will deliver the greatest value. It provides greater confidence when deciding which assets continue to perform effectively, where upgrades are required and how infrastructure investment can be prioritized over time.
For organizations operating large and complex infrastructure estates, this is becoming increasingly important. Every investment decision carries an opportunity cost, making it essential to understand where resources will have the greatest impact. Better operational insight provides the evidence needed to support those decisions while helping organizations maximize the value of the infrastructure they already own.
It also contributes to wider organizational objectives. Targeted preventative maintenance can reduce unnecessary site visits, improve the efficiency of engineering teams and support sustainability ambitions by reducing travel and extending the useful life of assets where appropriate.
Understanding infrastructure will define its future
The debate about critical infrastructure often focuses on what needs replacing. In reality, the bigger opportunity lies in making better use of what already exists.
Organizations that combine connectivity, operational data and engineering expertise will be able to make better decisions about maintenance, investment and long-term asset management. They will improve resilience, extend asset life and deliver stronger outcomes without relying solely on large-scale capital programs.
Intelligent Infrastructure gives operators the insight to act earlier, invest with greater confidence and make better use of the assets they already own. Over time, that leads to more resilient networks, longer asset life and better outcomes for the customers and communities that rely on them.
